167befz9bdb4g.technology: crane copy + crane validate --remote (RESTORE); curl + jq GET/HEAD over /v2/ (INVENTORY) — both via cloudflared access tcp
167befz9bdb4g.title: RESTORE path, added 2026-08-05 (#7277/ADR-169). After the recut destroys the store, a needs:-chained job copies the required pin set GHCR -> zot over the CF Tunnel bridge and verifies each reference's BLOBS with crane validate --remote, not just its manifest — zot gc can evict a layer, so a digest-only check goes green on an image no host can pull (measured). Rehearsed against a throwaway zot in the runner BEFORE the destroy; that rehearsal is what authorizes the destroy at all. Fail-loud with one operator action per enumerated exit code; resumable, so a partial pass is recovered by re-running. SECOND, INDEPENDENT TRAVERSAL added 2026-08-06 (#7278/ADR-172) — the READ-ONLY INVENTORY sweep: registry-zot-inventory.yml walks GET /v2/ -> /v2/_catalog -> /v2/<repo>/tags/list -> /v2/<repo>/manifests/<ref> (+ index recursion and the referrers API) over the SAME cloudflared access tcp bridge, as the PULL user, with curl+jq and NOT crane (crane collapses every failure to exit 1, so the verdict taxonomy could not key on status codes, and it would move egress into a second binary). GET/HEAD only, asserted at the wire by a recording origin in the tests. It accumulates blob sizes DEDUPLICATED BY DIGEST — a naive per-tag sum multiplies every shared base layer and yields a number with no relationship to the disk. It reaches the bridge with skip-docker-login: true, so ZOT_PUSH_* is never materialized into the runner; the guarantee is NON-MATERIALIZATION, not non-possession (the job still holds a soleur/prd-root Doppler token that COULD read them — Doppler tokens are config-scoped, not secret-scoped — so the script asserts at entry that ZOT_PUSH_USER/ZOT_PUSH_TOKEN are unset and exits non-zero otherwise). The WRITE half of this surface is NOT reachable and must not be re-proposed as though it were: the deny-by-default accessControl grants the pull user ['read'] and the push user ['read','create','update'], so NO user holds 'delete' (measured) and manifest DELETE is refused whatever the pinned build implements. The INVENTORY is fired by workflow_dispatch only: manually, or (since #7377) by scheduled-zot-restart-loop.yml when it opens a NEW non-OOM restart-loop tracker. The label-triggered route that preceded it could never fire (a label applied with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow run) and was deleted. After the walk the enumerator reads one SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK heartbeat newer than its START row through betterstack-query.sh, so a restart or host replace during the sweep reaches the durable marker as reason=restart_during_sweep.

A producer-side change to the FSM's emit shape (the flag key, pinned by inngest-cutover-flip.test.sh), the timer cadence, or the vector.toml allowlist for that tag is a change to the cutover's own gate, and a warehouse-side change to the ingest parse surfaces there as fsm_unreadable — read the github -> betterstack edge for the consumer. 1h201sq0dwd47.title: Transport and root authentication LIVE (ADR-220 D1b accepted 2026-09-27). Reviewer-gated root SSH from git-data-cutover.yml (job `cutover`, environment web-platform-infra-apply, main only, serialized on git-data-state): through the ssh. tunnel to web-1 (10.0.1.10 via the bridge NAT rule), then a web-1 direct-tcpip channel (-W 10.0.1.20:22, literal target), authenticating end-to-end with the dedicated root key so no key or agent socket lands on web-1. The key is Terraform-minted in its own root (git-data-root-key), read at run time from the separate Doppler project soleur-git-data-root, and reaches the host only through a create of hcloud_server.git_data checked against a committed fingerprint. After the access gate the proof mode only reads the store (served by the LUKS mapper with its store marker bound, not frozen, empty) and the shape of its pre-receive fence, and exits. The flip, rollback, unfreeze and redeploy modes (#8211 PR2) write the freeze sentinel and clear it, write the prd flag through a windowed write token and redeploy the web fleet through the deploy webhook; the flip and the rollback end with a transactional probe over the same SSH path (provision, fenced push and remove with a synthetic id, zero residue) that proves erasure still works. The refs_assert mode (#11431, same job, store flag off) is read-only (it writes nothing to the store; the host session makes and removes one transient /dev/shm scratch directory): after the store probes one host session reads the replicated refs and prints counts and at most two commit ids, never a name. None of the cutover-job modes copies or mounts a volume: the store is born on LUKS (ADR-239) and rollback is flag-off only. Since #10138 the same environment, bridge and root key also serve a second root-SSH consumer, the `wipe` job (modes wipe_check, wipe, wipe_finish, snapshot_clear; the cutover job is skipped for them): its host verb (MODE=wipe_assert, one ssh session) writes nothing to the store or to the retired plaintext volume and prints fixed words and per-type counts only, never a name; wipe_finish and the post-detach read create nothing on the host, but in mode=wipe_check and mode=wipe the pre-detach read creates and removes one transient host-local device-mapper snapshot of the kernel read-only plaintext device (its copy-on-write file in RAM) and mounts that snapshot read-only to count top-level entry types, and mode=snapshot_clear removes a leftover one of those (no volume operation). No mode copies a volume, and the retired plaintext volume is deleted through the Hetzner API edge, never through the host. A failed, stranded or cancelled run is reported by the separate notify-failure job (an issue plus an ops email) and never by this edge. Host keys PINNED on both hops (ADR-237, accepted 2026-09-27): web-1 by its committed ECDSA-P256 pin, git-data by its Terraform-minted ED25519 key, rotated on every replace and published as the TF-owned prd secret GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY, which the flag precheck reads with the prd token it already holds. web-1 can no longer impersonate git-data; a pinned key authenticates the host, not its answers (ADR-220 amendment log). THE READ CREDENTIAL'S SCOPE CHANGES (#8209, ADR-241 D7), and it is the half ADR-220 explicitly deferred: DOPPLER_TOKEN_GIT_DATA_ROOT stops being a REPO secret — which any workflow on any branch of this PUBLIC repo could name, so 'reviewer-gated, main only' described the cutover JOB and never the credential — and becomes an ENVIRONMENT secret on web-platform-infra-apply under the SAME NAME. Same name deliberately: this workflow is #8211-owned and needs no edit, because its cutover job already declares that environment and an environment secret overrides a repo secret of the same name. The Terraform-minted token and the repo secret are FORGOTTEN by Terraform (removed blocks carrying lifecycle destroy = false, so both live objects keep serving until they are replaced — that is what makes the change safe to merge ahead of any out-of-band step), then revoked. The second path to the same key moves too: web-platform/git-data-root-key/terraform.tfstate, which the prd_terraform backend keys could read, relocates to the soleur-terraform-state-privileged bucket that only a bucket-scoped Tier-B token reads (see the github -> cloudflare edge). Both paths ADR-220's D4 'repo-secret reach' residual named are therefore closed AS TO BRANCH-WORKFLOW REACH, and NOT as to a prd repo-secret holder: that holder still reads the soleur-ai runtime key, whose App carries administration:write on jikig-ai/soleur and can rewrite the very deployment-branch policy the new carrier rests on. That is ADR-241 residual R1, filed at p1, and it is why ADR-241 D2 is `proposed` rather than `accepted` and why ADR-220's D4 residual is addressed but not closed

1vx5fvizmnn4r.title: deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000 (webhook) and ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22 — ORIGIN-RELATIVE to web-1's private IP since #6594/PR-A (was localhost:, the ADR-114 I2 anti-pattern). Whichever connector replica CF selects now proxies to web-1, the only host that serves these routes — so the edge is deterministic BY CONSTRUCTION (I2 discharged), not merely 'inert while one connector holds'. Matches the registry. edge, already origin-relative (10.0.1.30). /hooks/deploy still fans out to peers over the private net (ADR-068 Option B); deploy-status, inngest-liveness and infra-config do NOT fan out — with the origin-relative pin they no longer need to, since they answer from web-1 regardless of colo. DELIVERY IS NOT ACTIVATION (ADR-161, #7103): the infra-config route WRITES files, and systemd reads a drop-in only when its unit is (re)started — so until #7146 this edge delivered corrected vector/inngest-heartbeat drop-ins, reported ok, and left both units running the revoked credential they had been started with. The handler now restarts the units it configures and reports a per-unit verdict the CI gate adjudicates, graded on effect (ActiveState + an advanced ExecMainStartTimestamp) because try-restart exits 0 on a failed unit and, on Type=simple, means 'forked' rather than 'running'. THE DELIVERY↔ACTIVATION BOUNDARY IS infra-config-install.sh's drop-in shape gate, and it is load-bearing rather than hygienic: systemd merges drop-ins AFTER the unit body and vector.service runs User=deploy, so once anything on this route can root-restart a unit, an unvalidated *.service.d/*.conf becomes arbitrary execution (User=root, a replaced ExecStart=). The gate ships before the DROPIN_TRY_RESTART grant for that reason; the ordering is an invariant, not a preference. #7220 CORRECTS TWO THINGS HERE. (a) 'The handler now restarts the units it configures' was only half-true from #7146 until #7220: the handler's own `systemctl daemon-reload` ran as User=deploy with NO sudoers grant, returned 'Interactive authentication required', and set -e aborted AFTER all 19 files were written but BEFORE any unit was reconciled — so this edge delivered 19/19 files, published a frame of HARDCODED ZEROS naming nothing (files_total=0, restarts:[] — the EXIT trap's constants, not measurements), and activated nothing, for ~3 months. It did NOT report per-unit verdicts: the handler died before the reconciliation loop, so there was never a verdict to report — that absence is PR-A's whole narrative and the reason the CI gate read files_total=0 as 'delivered nothing'. The two drop-in-only units carry drop-ins in FILE_MAP and are absent from RESTART_MAP, so THIS channel never restarted them — but 'neither RESTART_MAP nor the grant set' was wrong: inngest-server IS in the grant set (INNGEST_RESTART/START/STOP/QUIESCE/ENABLE). The honest claim, and it is no softer: the HANDLER's reload never ran, so activation VIA THE CONFIG CHANNEL never happened for either unit. A second, co-located channel exists — ci-deploy.sh's `case inngest)` runs inngest-bootstrap.sh as root, which itself does daemon-reload plus `systemctl restart inngest-server.service` and the heartbeat units — so incidental reconciliation may have covered some units on some deploys, and the config channel had no way to know which. Unknown coverage, not proven staleness. (b) The boundary is now TWO gates, not one: the drop-in shape gate PLUS a *.service CONTENT PIN (exact sha256), because a reload grant lets systemd adopt a rewritten FULL unit and a permitted-directive grammar cannot bound a file whose job is to carry ExecStart=. Generalised invariant: every content gate ships before the grant that makes its file class ADOPTABLE — not merely before the grant that restarts it.

33ci096wc63n6.title: CI reaches the deny-all-public zot host to dual-push release images, and reaches web-1's shell for the 28 server.tf terraform_data SSH provisioners (27 plus the read-only web_1_host_key_probe, the count web-host-provisioner-parity.test.sh pins as FLOOR_RESOURCES; #12007 added host_kernel_marker_install and host_kernel_marker_install_web2, the latter reached by the same ssh -L forward through the pinned web-1 bastion as deploy_pipeline_fix_web2 with no new tunnel ingress, both operator-applied rather than delivered by the merge; #9151 added deploy_pipeline_fix_web2, which apply-deploy-pipeline-fix.yml reaches by an ssh -L 2223:<web-2-private>:22 forward THROUGH the pinned web-1 bastion plus a second OUTPUT REDIRECT — web-2's pinned host key on the connection block, no new tunnel ingress; #9534 added egress_gateway and egress_gateway_web2, both in apply-web-platform-infra.yml's SSH-stage target list, which opens no web-2 forward because the shared bridge redirects web-1 only) — both ONLY through this tunnel, via CF Access service tokens (separate tokens per route, so registry-write rotates independently of host-shell access). The ssh. hop also carries git-data-cutover.yml's jump to the git-data store (ADR-220). HOST KEY PINNED (ADR-237, #7226/#8125): web-1's ECDSA-P256 host key is a committed, reviewed pin (apps/web-platform/infra/web-1-ssh-host-key.pub, captured outside Cloudflare) that the bridge writes into a strict known_hosts for its bash callers and that every Terraform connection block sets as host_key, so neither the CF edge nor anything else can stand in for web-1; a mismatch fails closed. ACCESS AND TUNNEL ARE SEPARABLE AND THIS EDGE DEPENDS ON BOTH — a distinction this model otherwise elides (there is no distinct Access node; it lives only in edge descriptions like this one). ADMISSION is decided by CF Access at the edge; TRANSPORT is the tunnel. They fail independently, and the Access failure is the one that looks healthy: cloudflared connects, the local 127.0.0.1:2222 listener opens, and `nc -z` succeeds, because the service-token handshake is refused only when a connection is actually proxied. 2026-07-28 CAUSE CLASS (#7095), a SECOND instance of the token-rotation shape recorded on the registry. edge above but on the ssh. route: the ci_ssh Access service token was rotated out-of-band during incident response, and since Cloudflare returns client_secret ONLY at create, both Terraform state and Doppler went stale invisibly while `terraform plan` stayed clean. Run 30650564509 built this bridge, DESTROYED terraform_data.{infra_config_handler_bootstrap,deploy_pipeline_fix}, and only then failed on `ssh: handshake failed: connection reset by peer` — leaving state emptier than reality and production undeployable for 3 days on a host whose cx33 type had 0/6 datacenter stock, i.e. unreplaceable. GATED SINCE #7133 (ADR-154): the shared cf-tunnel-ssh-bridge composite's FINAL step asserts Access still admits the credential and fails with a named reason (ci_ssh_access_denied / ci_ssh_liveness_unverifiable / ci_ssh_liveness_unavailable) BEFORE any caller's terraform runs. Repair path is the ci-ssh-token-replace dispatch arm, never a host replace.

351viohfkymya.technology: cloudflared access tcp → raw TCP over WebSocket (tcp://, NOT http:// — #6122)
351viohfkymya.title: registry. ingress → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000. ORIGIN-RELATIVE — whichever connector replica answers proxies to the correct zot host, but ONLY if that replica is a 10.0.1.0/24 member (ADR-114 I1). #6416 (historical): web-2 was not a subnet member, so CI's registry bridge failed and the zot mirror silently skipped (masked green by continue-on-error). web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538); the surviving web-1 connector is a subnet member, so this failure mode is closed. 2026-07-29 CAUSE CLASS (#7071) — a DIFFERENT failure on this same edge, recorded so the closed #6416 mode above is not re-derived as the explanation: CI's bridge failed with websocket: bad handshake, and THAT TIME the cause was the EDGE refusing the upgrade (CF Access rejecting a rotated service token), NOT a missing origin route — a missing route would handshake and fail origin-side. Root cause: every doppler_secret carrying a token declares lifecycle{ignore_changes=[value]}, so Terraform REPLACED the registry_push Access service token and could never propagate the new value; the stale one was still being served. Detected by scripts/check-cloudflare-token-drift.sh, now wired into scheduled-terraform-drift.yml + a release preflight. 2026-08-03 THIRD CAUSE CLASS (#7242) — this record's dichotomy (edge-refusal vs missing-route) was NOT exhaustive, and reading it as exhaustive is what misdirected the next investigation. A bad handshake means only that the tunnel could not complete an ORIGIN DIAL. Third case, measured: the route was present AND Access ADMITTED the request, but the origin was RESTARTING — zot crash-looping at ~4/min, which a tens-of-seconds docker login + three-tag crane copy is near-certain to straddle. The Access policy was intact and the connector had never dropped. So bad handshake is a SYMPTOM, never a cause: since #7242 the failing step branches on a verdict the job measured (scripts/zot-mirror-diagnosis.sh, ADR-166) rather than naming one. NOTE also that a plain HTTPS GET here returns an empty 200 BY DESIGN (tcp:// ingress is not a WS upgrade) and is not a health probe.

Issue alerts route to email → target_type issue owners with fallthrough_type ActiveMembers; a few rules set fallthrough_type NoOne instead (issue-alerts.tf is the authoritative list). Every rule is a `sentry_alert` carrying the route as `action_filters[].actions[].email` with a lowercase `target_type = issue_owners`; since #8451 the two rules whose `event_unique_user_frequency_count` trigger the pinned provider cannot express (`auth_per_user_loop` and `sandbox_startup_failure`) are FROZEN `sentry_alert` blocks (`legacy_trigger_conditions`, `ignore_changes = all`), no longer `sentry_issue_alert`. `scripts/sentry-alert-live-fidelity.sh` checks every `sentry_alert` field-for-field against the plan-derived reference (#8050) after each apply and daily. One further rule is live in the project and ABSENT FROM IaC: the Sentry-default `Send a notification for high priority issues` — empty filters, null environment, NotifyEmailAction with target_type IssueOwners and fallthrough_type ActiveMembers. Its conditions are New/ExistingHighPriorityIssueCondition, i.e. FIRST-SEEN and ESCALATED-TO — NOT a recurrence of an issue that is already high priority. Since Sentry derives high priority from level, it is what actually routes a level=error event carrying no matching tag filter (the release-outcome mirror among them), and a repeat of an identical event is silent on this route. It is UI-managed, so ADR-031's IaC-is-the-source-of-truth posture does not cover it; tracked as #7142. NB IssueOwners has no ownership rule on this project, so the fallthrough is what actually reaches a human: a NoOne rule fires and pages nobody, by design only where issue-alerts.tf says so and a defect anywhere else. The cron monitors open an issue on a missed/failed check-in (per-monitor failure_issue_threshold). Since #8630 those issues reach email through one more `sentry_alert`, `cron_monitor_failure` in cron-monitor-alerts.tf, which binds every routed cron detector in `monitor_ids` (first-seen, reappeared and regression triggers; at most one email per monitor per 24 h) with the same issue_owners → ActiveMembers route. A MUTED monitor environment creates no issue, so it pages nobody even though it is routed; mute is not expressible in the provider. The uptime monitors open an issue on downtime, but their detectors are bound to no workflow, so this edge claims no route for them

9kpu4xmy19ky.title: Tier-B Terraform credentials (#8209, ADR-241 D2/D3): a Tier-B job loads the WHOLE soleur-infra-privileged/prd project through .github/actions/infra-credentials, using a read service token that is a GitHub ENVIRONMENT secret (DOPPLER_TOKEN_INFRA_PRIVILEGED) on an environment whose deployment-branch policy admits `main` ONLY — infra-privileged (no reviewers, for the unattended apply-on-merge and drift paths and, since #9262, the inngest pin bump and auto-mint, and, since #9454 item 4, the weekly weakness-digest PR author), web-platform-infra-apply, inngest-cutover and workspaces-luks-cutover. Since #10138 the `wipe` job of git-data-cutover.yml (environment web-platform-infra-apply) is a loader consumer too, and the first one in that workflow: it calls the loader once, with only the Tier-B token (no legacy token), and every step after the loader runs under an exec env -i allow-list (ADR-241 amendment 2026-10-14). Since #10540 inngest-key-rotate.yml (environment infra-privileged, dispatch-only, ADR-307) is a loader consumer in its apply1, apply2 and reboot jobs; its guard job holds the Tier-A token only, and its redeploy job holds the deploy webhook credentials only. Since #11294 key-rotate.yml (environment infra-privileged, dispatch-only, ADR-317) is a loader consumer in its apply and clear jobs: its guard, redeploy and notify jobs hold no Doppler credential (the guard reads the GitHub API only, the redeploy job names the deploy webhook credentials in one step, the notify job holds the issues scope). The boundary is the BRANCH POLICY, not the reviewer gate: GitHub evaluates it before the job starts and before the secret is materialized, which is the one thing a repo secret cannot do (any workflow on any branch of this PUBLIC repo can name a repo secret, and that is how DOPPLER_TOKEN_TF, HCLOUD_TOKEN, CF_API_TOKEN_R2 and a soleur-ai App key became branch-reachable). A PROJECT, never a prd_* branch config: a branch config resolves its root's secrets, which is how prd_terraform inherited prd. Terraform declares the project and its environment and mints NOTHING into them — the web-platform root's state is Tier-A readable, so a doppler_secret or doppler_service_token declared there would land in exactly the tier this edge exists to evict it from; the containers are IaC, the values are supplied out of band. Every doppler run in a Tier-B job carries --preserve-env, so a value planted in the Tier-A-writable prd_terraform can never shadow a loaded Tier-B value (doppler run OVERRIDES the environment by default; the flag is what makes precedence a property of the code). Enforced on every PR by tests/scripts/test-infra-privileged-tier-census.sh, which derives the Tier-B job set from references to the secret and the environment set from what those jobs declare, never from a hand-kept list. NOMINAL UNTIL R1: a holder of a prd repo-secret token still reads the soleur-ai runtime key, whose App carries administration:write on jikig-ai/soleur and can therefore rewrite the branch policy this edge rests on — which is why ADR-241 D2 is `proposed`, not `accepted`. SINCE #8609 (ADR-241 D10) the project also carries GITHUB_APP_RUNTIME_DOPPLER_TOKEN, the web host's read token for the isolated soleur-github-app project (see the doppler -> hetzner edge). It is operator-minted into Tier B, never Terraform-minted (ADR-241 D3). The loader always exports its TF_VAR_ name and fills it only for the jobs that opt in (the deploy-pipeline push and the web-host create/replace jobs), so the Tier-A prd_terraform arm can never supply it. R1 is CLOSING with this mechanism; the NOMINAL clause above holds until the old key's JWT gets 401 (runbook R7) and D2 flips. SINCE #9262 two unattended App-token consumers on infra-privileged — build-inngest-bootstrap-image.yml's bump-cloud-init-pin and mint-inngest-bootstrap-tag.yml's mint — and, since #9454 item 4 (ADR-285), a third, weakness-miner.yml's open-pr, which mints a contents+pull_requests token to author, push and arm the weekly digest PR as the App, do NOT load the project through infra-credentials: the ./.github/actions/mint-infra-app-token composite makes a single-key read of GITHUB_INFRA_APP_ID and GITHUB_INFRA_APP_PRIVATE_KEY (doppler secrets get with --project and --config prd in argv, the project one of two validated names). SINCE #9321 (ADR-241 D11) those consumers read the NARROW Doppler project soleur-infra-app/prd, which holds a copy of only the two App values (Terraform declares the empty project; an operator-run script copies the values and mints its read token) and is reached with a read token that is the environment secret DOPPLER_TOKEN_INFRA_APP, so none of those jobs holds the whole-project token or can reach GITHUB_APP_RUNTIME_DOPPLER_TOKEN. The composite's one broad-source caller, apply-github-infra.yml, names the whole project explicitly and keeps DOPPLER_TOKEN_INFRA_PRIVILEGED, which it already holds for Terraform. The narrowing is least privilege by reference under the main-only policy, not a boundary against a change merged to main

gxkkp0qf6t0l.title: Injects the web-host boot credential. The LUKS-at-rest passphrase (WORKSPACES_LUKS_KEY, ADR-119) is deliberately scoped to a DEDICATED prd_workspaces_luks config read by a read-only host token — NOT the shared soleur/prd config. Rationale is host-vs-CONTAINER, not host-vs-host (web-1 already carries full-prd, so there is no host blast radius left to buy): cloud-init runs `doppler secrets download --config prd` into the TMPENV that feeds `docker run --env-file`, so a key in shared prd would be readable via /proc/self/environ by the very agent code whose data it encrypts (CWE-522). The #6649 header-escrow R2 S3 creds (WORKSPACES_HEADER_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) + bucket name + endpoint are delivered via the SAME prd_workspaces_luks scoped read for web-1; never on the cutover's sudo argv. Web-class hosts born after #9397 read the separate prd_workspaces_luks_web config instead, so their token does not read web-1's escrow pair (the pre-split token still exists and still reads it until it is retired). Since #9123 the scoped read also runs on EVERY BOOT (workspaces-luks-reopen.service fetches WORKSPACES_LUKS_KEY via `doppler secrets get --plain --config prd_workspaces_luks` and pipes it to `cryptsetup luksOpen --key-file -`), which makes this Doppler read a STORE-AVAILABILITY dependency of every web-1 boot (and, once a fresh host has been converted to the guest-side LUKS path of ADR-263, of every boot of that host too) — the same trade #8210 accepted for git-data: a Doppler outage at boot leaves the mapper closed, the nofail boot proceeds degraded with docker held by RequiresMountsFor (site down, data-safe), and an exhausted restart ladder reports once, off-host, at level:fatal via op=workspaces-luks-drift (success is journald-only — an emit on the healthy path would page on every boot). SINCE #8609 (ADR-241 D10) the web host also reads a SECOND, ISOLATED project: the soleur-ai runtime App key (GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) lives in the Doppler project soleur-github-app (config prd), NOT in soleur/prd, read by a DEDICATED read-only service token (web-host-github-app-read) that rides one conditional line (GITHUB_APP_DOPPLER_TOKEN) of the existing /etc/default/soleur-doppler-token render. ci-deploy.sh and the boot path download prd as before, then overlay exactly that one name from the isolated project, and only for a cosign-verified @sha256 image; the canary proves GitHub accepts the key (GET /app, slug soleur-ai) before promotion. A project, not a prd_* branch config, so no prd/prd_* reader can see the key; until the runbook's R6 evicts it, prd still holds the old key as the fallback. Sequence: infra-credential-tiers-8209.md, section Runtime App key (#8609). A FRESH web host (web-2) gets its own scoped read-only token for the separate prd_workspaces_luks_web config (doppler_service_token.workspaces_luks_fresh_boot_web, ADR-263 D4 as amended by D7; the superseded workspaces_luks_fresh_boot token, scoped to prd_workspaces_luks, is unreferenced and awaiting an acknowledged destroy) delivered in user_data and written to /etc/default/luks-monitor, never co-rotated with web-1's token (its rotation IS a host replacement). Like every prd_* branch-config token it resolves about 116 prd secrets, so the passphrase is isolated from the container env file but not from a holder of this token, and it cannot be revoked after first boot because the reopen unit reads it on every boot; containers are default-drop firewalled from the metadata endpoint, host-side docker-group users are root-equivalent. Since PR #9448 (Ref #9377, merged 2026-10-04) the key exists: a manual dispatch of apply-web-platform-infra.yml (now disabled_manually) created it and the escrow bucket at 14:35 UTC on 2026-10-04. The single-use escrow-create workflow that once planned against them is retired, so a create of the web-class passphrase (random_password.workspaces_luks_web) is refused by the apply HALT with no replacement route (#9372); the push-apply can still create the Doppler key copy, the config, the bucket and the name secrets, and a create there is not halted. The web-2 volume rebirth (#9372) was a dispatch-only, single-use workflow (web2-luks-rebirth.yml, run on 2026-10-06 and deleted 2026-10-12): it deleted web-2's plaintext volume (judged empty on a size bound) through the Hetzner API and replaced the host so the provisioner formats a raw volume LUKS at first boot. The two R2 credential names (the operator mint) were still absent that day, and the readiness preflight refuses a birth until they exist. A web-class host born after that reads its OWN WORKSPACES_LUKS_KEY from prd_workspaces_luks_web, defined independent of web-1's, so its token will no longer read web-1's passphrase; this is narrowed, not proven isolated (one Doppler project, one Terraform state, one provider token), and the pre-split token still reads web-1's passphrase until it is retired (ADR-263 addendum 2026-10-03)

s79tukw6hgh2.technology: curl → Better Stack Logs + heartbeats (HTTPS, eu-fsn-3)
s79tukw6hgh2.title: Ships disk-state observability — df% of /var/lib/zot + resize2fs before/after + zot health — as one SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK event, plus a SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC private-NIC convergence event (#6415), to the SHARED Logs source 2457081; token in soleur-registry/prd, queried via betterstack-query.sh --grep SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK|SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC (#6244/#6415). SOURCE 2457081 IS NOT ISOLATED TO THIS HOST — the web hosts and the Inngest node ship to the SAME source (see the hetzner and inngest edges), and an earlier version of this description called it 'the isolated Logs source', contradicting those edges. Rows are told apart only by a per-host discriminator, and on THIS edge that discriminator is an IN-MESSAGE host= token, never the host_name FIELD: host_name is Vector-populated and this host runs no Vector, so a direct curl POST carries none. SINCE #7440/ADR-184 THIS EDGE ALSO CARRIES THE ZOT CONTAINER LOG STREAM. a 5-minute /etc/cron.d/zot-log-shipper one-shot (NOT a daemon — ADR-184 §4 rejects Restart=always on this host because it has no in-place execution path, so every daemon failure mode costs a destructive replace) reads journald CONTAINER_NAME=zot (the container already runs --log-driver journald, so this was a SHIPPING gap, not an instrumentation one) and POSTs each line envelope-stamped as `SOLEUR_ZOT_LOG shipper=zot-log-shipper host=<hostname> <sanitized line>`, plus SOLEUR_ZOT_LOG_DROPPED rate-cap accounting rows and a one-shot SOLEUR_ZOT_LOG_BOOT delivery marker. Before it, the ONLY registry observability was the 5-min heartbeat, which samples one log line per interval — so every count derived from it was a LOWER BOUND, and a 6h measurement on 2026-08-11 found 72 rows for this host, all 72 heartbeats, with ZERO genuine zot log lines ever having reached the warehouse. ALSO pushes two distinct absence-based heartbeats, whose scopes must not be conflated: the 900s disk beat pings on df alone, so it alarms HOST death but stays green with zot dead; the 60s liveness beat (zot-liveness-heartbeat.timer, #6537) pings ONLY while zot answers on the host's own PRIVATE IP — never loopback, since zot binds 0.0.0.0 and loopback answers on a NIC-less host (#6400). That 60s beat doubles as the container-log channel's free positive control: zot logs every request at info, so a genuine zot line lands every minute BY CONSTRUCTION (~1,440/day), traversing the whole path a shipper-emitted canary would skip. The liveness beat's monitor is armed (#6537's feeder shipped; up/unpaused, re-measured 2026-09-24); consumer-perspective reachability is BUILT (#6438 §1): each web host runs web-zot-consumer-probe against its own per-host heartbeat (see the hetzner -> zotRegistry edge). SINCE #7270 THE HEARTBEAT ALSO SAYS WHY THE LIVENESS BEAT WAS WITHHELD: the feeder keeps per-boot counters in tmpfs after every beat, and SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK carries them in its trusted region as liveness_miss_cum, liveness_ping_fail_cum, liveness_ok_cum, liveness_late_ok_cum and liveness_last_miss_code, with no new token or egress on the feeder. It reaches the host through the registry-host replace that registry-host-replace-dispatch fires on the merge (#8361, the size-limit blocker named below, closed 2026-09-20). DO NOT LOOK FOR A HOST-SIDE SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY EMITTER — THERE IS NONE. That marker lands on the same source 2457081 but is emitted by GITHUB ACTIONS (see the github -> betterstack edge), not by this host, and it reads the token from soleur/prd rather than this host's isolated soleur-registry/prd copy. Note what that does NOT imply any more: the reason USED to be that a host-side emitter needs a REPLACE and no safe replace existed while the LUKS recut was unfired, but the recut HAS fired (pcent 100 -> 8 across 2026-08-04 -> 2026-08-10) and ADR-184 §6 retires that blocker, so CI-side emission is no longer the only near side of the deadlock. The inventory marker stays CI-side because a runner can compute a catalog-wide enumeration the host cannot, not because the host is uninstrumentable. A host-side change still applies NOTHING at merge (cloud-init-only, ADR-096) and waits for the next provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and still governs the NEXT such change. This shipper, however, is no longer waiting: DELIVERED 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z by a DEDICATED registry-host-replace (run 31639782781), and the earlier wording here — that delivery rides the step-6 registry-host-replace of the zot-pin ordered path — is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as falsified by ORDERING rather than by being wrong when written. That step-6 replace had already fired atomically inside registry-luks-recut on 2026-08-10T22:08Z, ~45h BEFORE this shipper merged (2026-08-12T19:38Z), so it carried nothing and the shipper sat inert on a host born before it existed. A rider is only valid while its vehicle is still pending. First PASS was read back OUT of the warehouse at 2026-08-12T21:03:51Z (37 envelope rows against a floor of 7, boot_marker present), which flipped ADR-184 adopting -> accepted. SINCE #8386 THE HEARTBEAT ALSO CARRIES THE STORE'S AT-REST POSTURE: store_mount_src, store_backing_dev, store_mount_devid, store_expected_devid and store_luks, all placed AHEAD of the free-text zot_last_err tail so they sit in the trusted region a consumer may parse. This is what makes hcloud_volume.registry's LUKS claim measurable off-box — before it, the claim rested on one 2026-08-10 registry_luks_recut job log and nothing observed whether the mapper reopened after any later replace. UNDELIVERED AT MERGE: it reaches the host only through a registry-host replace, blocked while #8361 keeps apply-web-platform-infra.yml over the workflow-file size limit.. HELD, NOT POSTED TODAY (#12007, ADR-322 addendum 2026-11-08 and its #12007 fix round): the registry does NOT post `SOLEUR_HOST_KERNEL` today. The registry-side emitter (a 6-hourly stamp-gated block in zot-disk-heartbeat.sh reusing the existing post() sender) ships in a separate owner-approved follow-up PR (#12386), because merging a change to cloud-init-registry.yml auto-fires registry-host-replace-dispatch.yml (ADR-190) and replaces the production registry host. The collector's `--role registry` support and the helper and feeder decode (identity is the in-message pair role=registry plus host=, both required, because this host runs no Vector) are already in place, so the registry stays `unknown` in the cve-exposure skill until that follow-up merges

xk2aw9ze5kta.title: Stores every user's checked-out repository. Mounted at /mnt/data and bind-mounted into the app container as /workspaces (cloud-init.yml). The app container is the SOLE writer, which is what makes a container stop a sufficient freeze for the ADR-119 cutover — though `docker stop` defaults to a 10s grace then SIGKILL, so the cutover uses -t 120 plus interrupted-write asserts: a truncated file is otherwise rsynced and certified correct. Since #9123 the mount is owned by PID 1 through fstab (/dev/mapper/workspaces … defaults,nofail) after a boot-time Doppler-keyed luksOpen by workspaces-luks-reopen.service, and the ADR-119 §(e) gate is armed on web-1: docker.service.d carries RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/data + After=workspaces-luks-reopen.service and the covered root-disk /mnt/data inode is chattr +i, so nothing can write the bare root-disk dir while the mapper is absent

description.txt: A beta tester or prospect the operator is in sales/product conversations with. The origin of the third-party contact + conversation PII captured in the owner-private beta-CRM (beta_contacts / interview_notes). An involuntary data subject (Art. 14); no direct access to the store.
Slack workspace — Better Stack incident-alert target (native integration); mobile push to the operator is the primary wake path, email retained as secondary (#9168, ADR-260).

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.
Vendors, regulators, and counsel emailing the operator address. Their statutory/operational mail is the email-triage inbox's inbound source.

A product end user asking app-help questions through the in-app support bubble. Reaches a scope-reduced support persona (ADR-113): cwd pinned to the deployed plugin root, read-only sandbox, `kb-search` as the only skill, and a Bash deny that records an escalation only on genuinely out-of-scope attempts. The persona answers via Read/Grep/Glob over the curated corpus — no shell (#9559).

An untrusted contributor opening a pull request. In CI their PR-head code executes only under pull_request isolation (fix-constraints Stage A: contents:read, no write token) and never in the privileged Stage B consumer, which opens a data-only draft follow-up PR from the default branch (ADR-074). The PR-head artifacts preflight executes on the operator's own workstation are plan-declared probes and checks (a discoverability probe, a founder-stated check). Each runs inside a bubblewrap sandbox with no credential stores bound and the repo read-only, failing closed if that sandbox cannot be established (ADR-175, ADR-275); a founder-stated check whose freeze does not trace to the local operator or to a reviewed copy on the default branch is shown and never run (a FAIL), and a freeze commit's author is a name anyone can type, so that anchor makes an override attributable and does not authenticate anyone. Their residual reach is host-loopback and outbound network (#7412). Other operator-side execution of a checked-out PR head (running its tests, its scripts, its hooks) is covered by NEITHER boundary.

The connected repo's own committed plugins/soleur/ dir, present in the user's workspace when they connect a Soleur-dogfooding repo. UNTRUSTED: its hooks/hooks.json command-hooks would run in the Node dispatch process (outside bwrap). INERT for the SDK — both real-SDK factories load plugins:[{path: getPluginPath()}] (the platform-deployed root), never this copy (ADR-093 trust boundary).

A workspace Owner using Soleur as their AI organization. Workspaces may have MULTIPLE Owners (ADR-038, ADR-073 team workspaces); Owner-shared surfaces (e.g. the operator email-triage inbox, ADR-066) are readable by every Owner, not just one founder.

Local Cursor CLI only. The founder loads this repository's Soleur plugin with agent --plugin-dir. Slice 1 registers no hook events and does not classify the session as cursor; hooks stay unwired until a measured guard port shows the CLI loads them. The IDE editor agent and Cloud Agents are outside this element (ADR-274).

Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2. ALSO (#8122, ADR-219): the UPSTREAM CONTENT SOURCE for every schema-conforming vendored bundle — goSprinto/compliance-skills (gdpr-gate rules) and General-Legal/legal-templates (legal-generate corpus, added here as the second upstream) — polled by cron-content-vendor-drift via the git/trees + git/blobs API against per-bundle NOTICE pins.

Loads the Soleur Codex plugin from its repository marketplace. Shares canonical skills and agent definitions through the harness adapter, with explicitly trusted lifecycle hooks. Repository setup adds rule loading and Bash guardrails; per-file Claude hook parity is not implied (ADR-215).

Devin CLI/Desktop locally and Devin Cloud sessions on Cognition-managed VMs. Loads the Soleur plugin in both: skills, AGENTS.md rules, and MCP carry; plugin subagents are local-only and plugin SessionStart/SessionEnd hooks never fire in cloud, so cloud sessions run under the Soleur Cloud Mode contract — sentinel-based classification (local | not-local:<reason>), capability banner, sequential-fallback review with Reviewed-Coverage disclosure, and a session-scoped acknowledgement gate before secrets or production mutation (#8159, ADR-221). On the LOCAL substrate Devin consumes BOTH `.claude/settings.json` and `.devin/config.json` hook registries with no cross-source dedup (measured, #8205 envelope capture); its tool wire names are lowercase (`exec`, `write`, `edit`, `ask_user_question`, `run_subagent`, `skill`), so Claude-canonical matchers in settings.json are loaded-but-dead under it — the repo's Devin hook set is bound in `.devin/config.json` with anchored matchers, per-hook dispositions are recorded in `.claude/hooks/devin-dispositions.tsv`, and `devin-matcher-parity.test.sh` is the drift guard (#8205, ADR-223).

Any unauthenticated reader of the public jikig-ai/soleur GitHub repository. Receives whatever automation publishes into issue bodies and comments. Not a data subject relationship — a PUBLICATION surface, and the one egress in this model that cannot be retracted once written.

Public npm registry hosting @soleur/opencode — the documented `npx @soleur/opencode install` delivery channel (#10723), published to by CI on every release. Auth is OIDC trusted publishing bound to jikig-ai/soleur + npm-publish.yml (ADR-310): the publish job's id-token exchanges for a repo+workflow-scoped credential; no long-lived NPM_TOKEN exists in CI (retired after the first green OIDC publish — the ~7-day granular-token expiry behind #11585's E404-masked-authz outage). npm masks publish-authz failures as 404 on PUT to an existing package.

jikig-ai/soleur-marketplace — a public repo holding ONLY .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, README and LICENSE (~39 KB). Its single plugin entry is a keyless, unpinned git-subdir source pointing at plugins/soleur in the monorepo, so an install materialises the plugin subtree alone (~10 MiB) instead of the whole repository. Its contents are OWNED BY TERRAFORM (#7493): github_repository_file.marketplace_manifest publishes the manifest from infra/github/soleur-marketplace-manifest.json in the monorepo, so the artifact carries that repo's CI (the always-run marketplace-manifest-guard context), its required checks and the CODEOWNERS pin on /infra/github/. A default-branch ruleset requires a PR with one approval and blocks deletion and force-push, bypassed only by the org admin, the Admin repo role and the soleur-ai App. That removes the DIRECT unreviewed push path for the two other org-wide contents:write Apps (claude, entire); it does not close them — they could still collude via PR-and-approve, and the ruleset governs this repo only, so the manifest is additionally protected at apply time by a ref guard and a tree-equals-main assertion in apply-github-infra.yml. Superseded: this element previously stated it had no CI, no review and no CODEOWNERS, with scheduled-marketplace-drift.yml as its only control. Since #7490 the drift workflow carries a second job that installs the published plugin in CI and asserts delivered content (ADR-182 Decision 6). KNOWN GAP (#9360): the CI apply writes as the soleur-infra App (loader infra mode since #8209 O3), which is not a bypass actor, so a manifest write is refused (409) until #9361 swaps the App bypass actor to soleur-infra.

The PUBLIC upstream surface of the Grype vulnerability scanner used by image-cve-scan.yml (W3, epic #9601): the pinned release tarball on github.com/anchore/grype (verified against a SHA256 literal in the workflow, the secret-scan.yml gitleaks pattern) and the vulnerability DB served from grype.anchore.io. The binary pin does NOT pin the DB (it changes daily); since slice 2a the scan verifies the downloaded archive against the checksum in the listing it fetched from the same host and imports it with auto-update off, recording the DB checksum, schema and build time per row. That is integrity and auditability, NOT authenticity (listing and archive share one origin), so a poisoned or stale DB remains a trust boundary: the DB-age check and the known-vulnerable canary stay as defences, and an unmeasured scan exits non-zero rather than reading clean.

The PUBLIC upstream registry (ghcr.io/project-zot/zot-linux-{amd64,arm64}) that publishes zot. Since #8714 step 5.3b-iii (2026-09-28) the registry host NO LONGER pulls from it: the zot-image-mirror workflow packages the exact upstream image (manifest D and every blob) into a GitHub release asset, and the host boots from that asset with ghcr.io name-resolution-denied (ADR-096 amendment 2026-09-28, part 2). So this node is now reached only by CI (the mirror build and the PR rehearsal), never by a host. Added 2026-08-05 (#7282) because the edge was unmodeled while the sibling ghcr node (our PRIVATE ghcr.io/jikig-ai/* packages) is DEAD on the pull path; reading the two as one node let a live dependency hide behind a dead one. Distinct trust boundary: third-party code, trusted at digest D; the asset sha256 T and config digest C in zot-registry.tf are re-derived from D on every PR (zot-image-mirror.yml rehearse), and the host refuses any other bytes. No cosign verification of the zot binary itself. No bot mutates the pin.

SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (#7640/ADR-194) — this CA does NOT issue the certificate the LIVE site is served with. SINCE the cutover (applied 2026-09-03) soleur.ai/www ARE served by Cloudflare Pages and terminate on the Cloudflare EDGE certificate (Google Trust Services); there is no origin leg, so no LE certificate sits anywhere on the serving path and this element must not be read as a live dependency of the apex. What survives is the RETAINED, DNS-DETACHED GitHub Pages path only, kept as the rollback TARGET — but note the narrowing that PR5 landed on 2026-09-03: a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback while the publish leg still ran; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin takes three acts (re-add the leg, redeploy, revert DNS) and a fourth if the apex still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES afterwards, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT is then also routing. Its LE certificate: its LE certificate is expired by construction and can never re-issue (eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast, which post-cutover it does not), and the remediation routine described below is DISARMED — gated on the live apex record type still being `A`, with its daily detector cron removed. Everything from here is the pre-cutover / rollback-path mechanism, unchanged and still correct for that path. ACME CA issuing the GitHub Pages custom-domain TLS cert for soleur.ai/www (ADR-125, #6657/#6698). Validation is HTTP-01 against GitHub's origin, which is why remediation must transiently flip apex+www to DNS-only — a Cloudflare-proxied record makes LE see CF anycast instead of GitHub's 185.199.x. TWO properties drive the design: (1) LE PREFERS IPv6 and retries over IPv4 only on a NETWORK-level failure of the first request (redirects get no retry), so a proxied AAAA that answers 200 with the wrong content defeats validation at any window length with no fallback — the propagation gate therefore requires AAAA ENODATA and treats a surviving AAAA as terminal, not retryable; (2) failed-validation rate limits are 5 per identifier per account per hour, refilling ~1 per 12 min with a compounding daily cap, and GitHub surfaces NONE of it — `GET /pages` returns the same `bad_authz` string whether the cause is DNS, timing, or a rate-limit pause. That invisibility is why probe-only mode (which consumes no validation attempt) is the DEFAULT for manual fires.

Claude LLM for agent reasoning and tool use. Operator keys are partitioned by blast radius into spend-limited Console workspaces (ADR-244, #8505): once the merge applies, CI and manual evals bill the soleur-ci-eval workspace ($100/month cap) instead of the prd key; production crons and the email-triage summarizer bill the prd key, except scheduled-machinery-drain.yml, which a production cron dispatches onto the CI key; end users bill their own BYOK keys. The prepaid balance is org-wide.

The unenumerated set of public HTTPS hosts an entitled workspace's agent session may CONNECT to through the egress gateway (#9534, ADR-278) — documentation, package registries, third-party APIs, chosen by the agent at run time. NOT a recipient/sub-processor in the Art. 28 sense: destinations are owner-directed, and the gateway's audit log attributes each CONNECT to the workspace token. The risk is disclosed at the toggle and accepted by name in the DPIA screening.

DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner. Since #11181/PR #11766 it also carries the GA LOAD BALANCER on app.soleur.ai (ADR-068 §(b)): cloudflare_load_balancer.app overlays the retained A record (fallback for a disabled LB), default+fallback pool web_1 {web-1@1 serving, web-2@1 serving since the 2026-11 serve flip (#12167); drain is an explicit ga-pool-update act}, health monitor http/:80 /health (the Flexible-SSL edge path; the https/:443 create shape probed a port with no listener and reported every origin down under the self-fallback), origin_steering random, plus a load_balancing_health_alert notification policy. Updates ride cf-lb-overlay.yml ga-monitor-fix/ga-pool-update arms — never the routine apply.
Centralized secrets management with runtime injection
Community notifications and release announcements
Payment processing and subscription billing

The operator's own per-user systemd manager, reached over the D-Bus socket at /run/user/<uid>/bus (SO_PEERCRED-authenticated, same uid only, no network). Owns the cgroup v2 hierarchy for the login session: the Hook Engine asks IT to create the memory-capped transient scope each agent session runs in, so systemd stays the SINGLE WRITER to that hierarchy and no component writes cgroup directories directly (ADR-161). Units are transient and self-clean when their last process exits, so nothing is provisioned and nothing persists across a reboot.

@playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha), spawned by npx as a stdio JSON-RPC child — one newline-terminated JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (measured) — driving a HEADED real Chrome (channel chrome, chromiumSandbox true, X11 forced at the env level) on the operator workstation with the persistent profile ~/.cache/playwright-mcp-profile (this repository's registration claims it, or a numbered sibling directory when it is held, by a kernel flock tied to the proxy process — slot 0 may wait up to 7 s, for the same session's previous launch or an unknown/unreadable owner — so a new-style launch or /mcp reconnect kills nothing; an old-style launch string still running in another worktree can, and the plugin registration has no lease), whose password manager autofills into pages the agent opens. An accessibility snapshot serialises the VALUE of every input, so a bare browser_snapshot on a login page or a credential panel returns the value inline in the tool result. Since #7980 the agent runtime reaches this server THROUGH the plugin's snapshotGuard component rather than directly — that relay is the trust boundary this node exists to show — and only on a registration that routes through it: this repository's .mcp.json does, and since #8156 the plugin's own plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registration does by default (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*, on the dedicated soleur-playwright-mcp-profile under the XDG cache root — that registration ships NO config and no display forcing, so it runs the upstream defaults: headed, channel chrome; on a host with no Google Chrome executable its opt-in --chromium-fallback proxy flag makes the proxy append --browser chromium --sandbox, so Playwright launches its bundled Chromium instead with the Chromium sandbox kept on (a host that cannot run it fails closed: install Google Chrome), and its env carries only PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS=0, an inert guard on stdio, not the fix for anything — ADR-271); a customer's own registration does not unless they route it themselves; the hosted agent-runner registers no Playwright server (the vendored plugin tree excludes the plugin-root .mcp.json — both vendor steps rm it post-copy, so the hosted plugins:[type local] load never discovers it); the Inngest fleet's per-fire cron-ux-audit overlay runs a SEPARATE 0.0.75 copy, UNWRAPPED, with --snapshot-mode none appended directly (register PA-31 §(g)). Every behaviour cited is a dated observation of the pinned version, not an undertaking about the tool; the suite derives its fixture directory from the pin, so a bump without a re-capture reddens.
Privacy-focused website analytics

Inbound email ingress (operator-inbox webhook, svix-verified) + transactional outbound (statutory triage notifications). Also the PUSH-FAILURE FALLBACK channel: a statutory push that reaches fewer than all devices falls back to Resend email (ADR-136, #6802). ADR-066.

FCM / APNs / WNS — the endpoint host each push_subscriptions.endpoint resolves to. Web Push delivery is transport-accepted (a 201), NOT proof of receipt (ADR-136). Non-410 failures do not prune the subscription and fall back to Resend email; the egress firewall's deliberate WNS DROP (#5046 PR-2) is the known trigger.

PRIVATE GHCR registry (ghcr.io/jikig-ai/soleur-web-platform + soleur-inngest-bootstrap) — the ORIGINAL host pull source, now WRITE-ONLY: still dual-pushed by CI, but DEAD AS A FALLBACK since the Phase-5 retirement — the read PAT is revoked (GET api.github.com/user -> 401) and the minter was disabled (GHCR_MINTER_DISABLED=true; pull-token mint -> 403 DENIED), verified 2026-07-30 (#7071); the minter, the PAT variables and their Doppler keys were deleted by ADR-096 task 5.4 (#8714). It receives every image and can serve none of its PRIVATE packages TO HOSTS (the host pull of the PUBLIC cosign verifier image was a separate edge until #8714 moved it to gcr.io — `hetzner -> sigstore`). Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. SINCE #8036 1c (2026-09-23) THE DEPLOY-PATH HOST-SIDE CODE IS DELETED, not merely dead, AND SINCE #8036 1d (2026-09-24, ADR-096 5.3b-i) THE FRESH-BOOT CODE TOO: no host presents a GHCR credential at boot — the web and inngest templates and the baked bootstrap script carry no GHCR login and no GHCR pull, and no templatefile() passes the GHCR credential into user_data (true of the templates at merge; of each host once it is replaced from them). The inngest templates keep the ghcr.io/…soleur-inngest-bootstrap tag@sha256 literal only as the bump bot's pin carrier; it is never pulled. ci-deploy.sh has no `docker login ghcr.io`, no auth-recovery re-fetch and no fallback branch, and it sweeps the revoked inline credential out of the deploy docker config on every deploy. So “dead edge” is now a statement about code that no longer exists rather than about a credential that cannot authenticate. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION (#11424, ADR-096 amendment 2026-10-28): soleur:registry-breakglass-mirror is the sanctioned MANUAL exception — an operator-driven break-glass pull that presents an operator-supplied read:packages PAT and scopes name resolution per-command via `curl --resolve` past the hosts-file sinkhole (zero persistent config, no standing credential, no host code path), so “dead edge” names the absence of a STANDING pull capability and is not absolute against a deliberate human procedure. Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).

The PUBLIC upstream release surface (github.com/inngest/inngest) that publishes the self-hosted `inngest` binary — release tags, per-arch tarballs (inngest_<ver>_linux_{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz), and one release-shipped checksums.txt per version. Reached by two consumers with different trust semantics: the dedicated host's bootstrap downloads the version the committed `inngest_cli_version` pin names and sha256-verifies the tarball against the committed per-arch checksum before executing it (the reviewed embed in inngest.tf is the trust anchor, not the checksums file — it is a plain sha256sum manifest, not GPG-signed), and CI reaches it twice (build-inngest-bootstrap-image.yml downloads the same pinned tarball for the bootstrap image; the `Detect inngest CLI pin drift` poll in rule-audit.yml reads the releases listing to measure the pinned-version delta, #7463). Added 2026-09-29 (#7463) because the edge was unmodeled while the pin sat 29 stable releases behind with no freshness owner — the gap #7308 named. FRESHNESS OWNER (mirrors the projectZot/node discipline): no bot mutates the pin; detection is the rule-audit.yml poll (1st + 15th — files one idempotent `inngest-pin-drift` issue); enforcement is apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-cli-staleness.test.sh in deploy-script-tests; the analysis of record is apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-cli.provenance.md; the sub-second liveness probe is inngest-cli-pin-probe.sh.

Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Google 8.8.8.8, queried via node:dns Resolver.setServers() by cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue's DNS-propagation gate (#6698). Used to confirm the DNS-only flip actually reached the public internet before the cert poll begins — Cloudflare's TTL for proxied records is fixed at 300 s, so a proxy-status flip takes ~5-10 min to propagate and a poll started before then is guaranteed-wasted public-TLS-outage window. `dig` is deliberately NOT used: it is not installed in the app image (the Dockerfile installs only ca-certificates, git, bubblewrap, socat, qpdf, jq), so shelling out would throw at runtime.

Runtime feature-flag service (ADR-038 v2, ADR-043): per-role segment overrides and per-feature `<flag>-orgs` segments, evaluated by the web app at request time with an env-var fallback mirrored in Doppler. Production writes (flag create/delete, role and org flips, user role traits) come only from the flag-* and user-set-role operator scripts, each gated on a typed `yes` at the founder's own terminal (ADR-249, #8486).

Keyless container-image signing/verification (cosign/Fulcio/Rekor). The release CI keyless-signs the pushed web app image digest (this IS a live sigstore call — github → sigstore below). The host then cosign-verifies the signature FULLY OFFLINE against a pinned trusted_root.json — it makes NO live sigstore call at verify time (ADR-087, #6005) — supply-chain authenticity for the shared host (#5933 Item 4).

The connected repo's own knowledge-base/ tree.
