description.txt: Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2. ALSO (#8122, ADR-219): the UPSTREAM CONTENT SOURCE for every schema-conforming vendored bundle — goSprinto/compliance-skills (gdpr-gate rules) and General-Legal/legal-templates (legal-generate corpus, added here as the second upstream) — polled by cron-content-vendor-drift via the git/trees + git/blobs API against per-bundle NOTICE pins.
Payment processing and subscription billing

The operator's own per-user systemd manager, reached over the D-Bus socket at /run/user/<uid>/bus (SO_PEERCRED-authenticated, same uid only, no network). Owns the cgroup v2 hierarchy for the login session: the Hook Engine asks IT to create the memory-capped transient scope each agent session runs in, so systemd stays the SINGLE WRITER to that hierarchy and no component writes cgroup directories directly (ADR-161). Units are transient and self-clean when their last process exits, so nothing is provisioned and nothing persists across a reboot.

Any unauthenticated reader of the public jikig-ai/soleur GitHub repository. Receives whatever automation publishes into issue bodies and comments. Not a data subject relationship — a PUBLICATION surface, and the one egress in this model that cannot be retracted once written.

Local Grok Build harness on the operator workstation. Loads plugins/soleur via .grok/config.toml (ADR-110, #8064). NOT Cloud CLI Engine: no Hetzner host, no api spawn, no Concierge/web edge (#6547 parked).

Claude LLM for agent reasoning and tool use. Operator keys are partitioned by blast radius into spend-limited Console workspaces (ADR-244, #8505): once the merge applies, CI and manual evals bill the soleur-ci-eval workspace ($100/month cap) instead of the prd key; production crons and the email-triage summarizer bill the prd key, except scheduled-machinery-drain.yml, which a production cron dispatches onto the CI key; end users bill their own BYOK keys. The prepaid balance is org-wide.

Inbound email ingress (operator-inbox webhook, svix-verified) + transactional outbound (statutory triage notifications). Also the PUSH-FAILURE FALLBACK channel: a statutory push that reaches fewer than all devices falls back to Resend email (ADR-136, #6802). ADR-066.

The PUBLIC upstream registry (ghcr.io/project-zot/zot-linux-{amd64,arm64}) that publishes zot. Since #8714 step 5.3b-iii (2026-09-28) the registry host NO LONGER pulls from it: the zot-image-mirror workflow packages the exact upstream image (manifest D and every blob) into a GitHub release asset, and the host boots from that asset with ghcr.io name-resolution-denied (ADR-096 amendment 2026-09-28, part 2). So this node is now reached only by CI (the mirror build and the PR rehearsal), never by a host. Added 2026-08-05 (#7282) because the edge was unmodeled while the sibling ghcr node (our PRIVATE ghcr.io/jikig-ai/* packages) is DEAD on the pull path; reading the two as one node let a live dependency hide behind a dead one. Distinct trust boundary: third-party code, trusted at digest D; the asset sha256 T and config digest C in zot-registry.tf are re-derived from D on every PR (zot-image-mirror.yml rehearse), and the host refuses any other bytes. No cosign verification of the zot binary itself. No bot mutates the pin.

The PUBLIC upstream surface of the Grype vulnerability scanner used by image-cve-scan.yml (W3, epic #9601): the pinned release tarball on github.com/anchore/grype (verified against a SHA256 literal in the workflow, the secret-scan.yml gitleaks pattern) and the vulnerability DB served from grype.anchore.io. The binary pin does NOT pin the DB (it changes daily); since slice 2a the scan verifies the downloaded archive against the checksum in the listing it fetched from the same host and imports it with auto-update off, recording the DB checksum, schema and build time per row. That is integrity and auditability, NOT authenticity (listing and archive share one origin), so a poisoned or stale DB remains a trust boundary: the DB-age check and the known-vulnerable canary stay as defences, and an unmeasured scan exits non-zero rather than reading clean.

Devin CLI/Desktop locally and Devin Cloud sessions on Cognition-managed VMs. Loads the Soleur plugin in both: skills, AGENTS.md rules, and MCP carry; plugin subagents are local-only and plugin SessionStart/SessionEnd hooks never fire in cloud, so cloud sessions run under the Soleur Cloud Mode contract — sentinel-based classification (local | not-local:<reason>), capability banner, sequential-fallback review with Reviewed-Coverage disclosure, and a session-scoped acknowledgement gate before secrets or production mutation (#8159, ADR-221). On the LOCAL substrate Devin consumes BOTH `.claude/settings.json` and `.devin/config.json` hook registries with no cross-source dedup (measured, #8205 envelope capture); its tool wire names are lowercase (`exec`, `write`, `edit`, `ask_user_question`, `run_subagent`, `skill`), so Claude-canonical matchers in settings.json are loaded-but-dead under it — the repo's Devin hook set is bound in `.devin/config.json` with anchored matchers, per-hook dispositions are recorded in `.claude/hooks/devin-dispositions.tsv`, and `devin-matcher-parity.test.sh` is the drift guard (#8205, ADR-223).

Public npm registry hosting @soleur/opencode — the documented `npx @soleur/opencode install` delivery channel (#10723), published to by CI on every release. Auth is OIDC trusted publishing bound to jikig-ai/soleur + npm-publish.yml (ADR-310): the publish job's id-token exchanges for a repo+workflow-scoped credential; no long-lived NPM_TOKEN exists in CI (retired after the first green OIDC publish — the ~7-day granular-token expiry behind #11585's E404-masked-authz outage). npm masks publish-authz failures as 404 on PUT to an existing package.

Write-once record of a founder's decision on a legal text (accept, decline, request changes), keyed by (founder uuid, key, text sha256), with a database-computed row checksum, plus the short-lived single-use email-code challenge behind a Yes (ADR-319, #12011). No foreign key: the pseudonymous founder uuid outlives the account (Art. 17(3)(e)). The founder records through the authenticated record_legal_acceptance RPC (actor from auth.uid(), only a web-session audience accepted, every decision needs a server-issued intent); the intent, the email-code challenge, the read-only check and the acknowledgement RPCs are service_role RPCs. A small acknowledgement table (legal_acceptance_ack: acceptance id and time only, no founder id, no note; pseudonymous personal data through its key) is written after the accepted event is flushed and read by the check endpoint to emit row_without_event. No agent tool writes the record and no agent tool reads the note: a runtime-audience token can neither read nor write it. The agent can read four fields about ONE decision (status, text_hash, decided_at, row_ok) through the bearer-gated check endpoint, which takes the founder id from its own configuration, and, through the sibling bearer-gated counts endpoint, a key's total and per-text-hash counts (no founder id, choice, time or note; the credential-free pre-publication aggregate, #12429, a service_role RPC listed in ADR-319); the note is not readable through the endpoint or any service_role path (a database-owner credential could read it; it is held by the operator and by the production migration pipeline, a CI secret, and no agent session is meant to use either; code holding the service key in-process is the stated ADR-319 residual). The Request changes note is read by pull only, by the operator personally, through an owner-level query in their own database login (founder -> legalAcceptanceStore below); nothing pushes it anywhere. The screens, the Inbox row and the decide and reauth routes answer only for the configured founder id (LEGAL_ACCEPTANCE_FOUNDER_ID; no configured id means off); the approval-queue flag is not read (ADR-319 amendment 2026-11-10); the check endpoint merges dark and answers 503 until its token and founder id are configured (PR-D).

nodes.title: Cloudflare Tunnel

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; that web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463). var.web_hosts has two keys again: a fresh cattle web-2 (10.0.1.11, #6969) was born 2026-07-27 after the gate merged. Since ADR-304 (2026-10-27, eMudhra advisory) it is the connector host — the role moved permanently off unreplaceable web-1; it is also a scheduler-less standby (runs the #8495 watchdog dispatch clock), web_colocate_inngest=false.) plugins/soleur/ — skills, agents, knowledge base, AND the shared bash primitives shipped for execution on an installed user's machine (ADR-178, #7409): scripts/lib/session-state.sh is the cross-session lock/lease layer that gates worktree reaping AND, since #8400, branch deletion: `cleanup-merged` keys its lease check on the BRANCH rather than on a worktree path, so a merged branch whose worktree was already removed is now held by a live lease instead of reaching `git push origin --delete` and `git branch -D`. The narrower wording was falsified by that change, in the same way and at the same time as the script's own fail-closed banner. It lived under .claude/hooks/ until #7409, i.e. outside the subtree marketplace.json copies, so every installed user ran with that layer silently replaced by no-op stubs. What this system SHIPS is therefore not only prose for an agent to read — it includes executable concurrency primitives whose absence is unobservable to the user. Since ADR-254 (#8880) it also ships a user-machine WRITE surface: `scripts/emit-decision.sh` appends field-allowlisted decision records to the project-local `.soleur/decisions.jsonl` (NO-ECHO metadata only, `.soleur/.gitignore` self-guard, ~5 MB rotation, tester-owned, no egress — the aggregate reaches Jikigai only when a tester runs `alpha-metrics.sh` and pastes it at checkpoint). Since ADR-264 it also ships the staged, agent-runnable operator-script contract (`scripts/lib/operator-script.sh`: --list, --stage, --stage --apply --plan-digest, exit 75) and the PreToolUse hook `hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh` registered in `hooks/hooks.json`, which reaches a founder's install and is loaded by web Concierge too (the web runtime opts it out until the web approval adapter lands). A further write surface lands with #9403 (ADR-268): `scripts/pipeline-tally.sh` mutates per-branch work-unit counters under `<git-common>/soleur-session-state/counters/` (key=value, flock-serialized, units only — never dollars) and `hooks/stop-hook.sh` READS the ledger's `capped` key as a hard-cap floor; the ledger is repo-local machine state with no egress, and ship renders its counts into the public PR body as a `## Pipeline Tally` section. Since ADR-250 Amendment 2 (#9677) `cleanup-merged` can also, on explicit opt-in, delete expired entries from the plugin's own scratch-quarantine directory under /tmp and /var/tmp (`SOLEUR_QUARANTINE_DRAIN=1`, a terminal delete on the user's machine scoped to that directory) and prune old Docker build cache and dangling images (`SOLEUR_DOCKER_PRUNE`, dry-run first, never volumes or containers); both print stdout markers (on a user's machine they stay there; the web platform's telemetry mirror forwards them like every other SOLEUR_* marker). Since ADR-277 (#9601, W2) it also ships a second PreToolUse hook, `hooks/destructive-command-guard.sh` (with the Perl lexer `hooks/lib/shell-argv.pl`), that asks or denies before a destructive terraform/tofu, default-branch force-push or recursive delete of `/` or home reaches a customer's shell; it sends nothing and writes nothing, and hosted web sessions opt it out through SOLEUR_DISABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD (server-side scheduled agents keep it active), so it protects customer-machine users, not hosted founders (hosted sessions ask separately, through a must-ask lane in canUseTool for common forms of a default-branch force-push or delete, terraform destroy and a gh delete, ADR-284; the lane does not recognise every spelling). Since ADR-290 Amendment 1 (#10331, slice 2) it also ships a user-repository surface: `plugins/soleur/scripts/lint-ratchet.py` user mode inspects any git repository it is run in (it reads root and tracked nested ruff configs and the baseline path, with no install and no ruff run unless a tracked ruff config AND a baseline file are present), and on an opted-in repository or an explicit --update executes a sha256-pinned ruff wheel it downloads once into a per-user 0700 cache outside the repository (PyPI over TLS, deliberately not modelled as an element); it writes `.lint-ratchet/ruff.baseline.txt` only on an explicit --update; it sends nothing to Soleur; the hosted image has no python3, so the call is a skip there.

Control ops are host-local (no cross-host forwarding). Lease in Postgres (ADR-068 user-sticky amendment)

Per-user worktrees are host-local in the ADR-068 §1 sense (they do NOT live on the shared git-data host) but they are NOT on the root NVMe — they sit on a per-host ATTACHED BLOCK VOLUME, workspacesVolume below (#6588 corrected this description, which said 'host-local NVMe' and led readers to conclude there was no volume to encrypt). At first boot a fresh host pulls the web app image from zot — digest-pinned refs only, with a baked endpoint + pull credential and a bounded private-NIC wait first (#8651, ADR-096 amendment 2026-09-23); before #8651 this pull was stuck on GHCR by a tokenless Doppler read (#6985) and went dark once the GHCR PAT was revoked — and extracts its baked bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl via docker cp (ADR-080, #5921) — a path web-1 can never take: the load-bearing reason is lifecycle{ignore_changes=[user_data]}, which means cloud-init never re-runs, so the bake reaches no live host (ADR-119 §(e)). ADR-143 (adopting, #6459) governs the return of a second web host: because cx33 was unorderable at the ADR-143 decision (2026-07-26 probe; still unorderable in hel1-dc2 on 2026-08-06, though it returned in nbg1-dc3/fsn1-dc14), web-2 returns as a fresh cattle **cpx22** (2c/4g x86, ~€19.49/mo net) — sized to web-1's MEASURED usage (~1.5 GB peak RAM / 0.48 load15 over 30d, not its over-provisioned 8g shape; ADR-143 D1) — a health-monitored standby at serving-weight 0 (NOT in the ingress rotation) until ADR-068 Phase-3 GA, since the sole-copy workspace volume lives on web-1 and a request routed to web-2 pre-flip would hit an empty workspace. TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-07-26 (ADR-143 addendum, #6966), FORCED BY STOCK: the live probe that day (/v1/datacenters .server_types.available) found the ENTIRE cx line — cx23 as well as cx33 — and the ENTIRE cax ARM line orderable in 0 of 3 EU DCs, so the earlier 'cx23, in stock in hel1' claim recorded here is FALSE and is retired. cpx22 matches cx23 on cores and RAM exactly (2c/4g) and doubles local disk, so the D1 sizing rationale is unchanged — this was a price change (+€14.00/mo), not a resize. Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. var.web_hosts now has two keys: web-2 was provisioned 2026-07-27 (#6969) and is a scheduler-less cattle standby (web_colocate_inngest=false — no inngest-server.service, no local reminders). web-2's own /workspaces volume is a different story from web-1's: web-1 keeps the additive LUKS singleton (hcloud_volume.workspaces_luks, ADR-119) delivered by its Terraform SSH installer, while a fresh host takes the baked guest-side LUKS path (ADR-263) - one mechanism, two Terraform addresses - and until web-2's live conversion has run it is still plaintext-but-empty, gate-blocked from serving weight and from holding user data. [Updated 2026-10-11 (#9372): its volume is now LUKS-formatted and opened; see the workspaces data-store note.]

nodes.title: browser-snapshot credential guard

description.txt: Four controls with one predicate (ADR-213 + its 2026-09-14 addendum, #7947/#7980): (1) redact-a11y-snapshot.py rewrites credential-NAMED input values in an accessibility tree to <redacted> — name-based, because no surface serialises type=; (2) browser-snapshot-credential-guard.sh, a PreToolUse DENY on any Bash-invoked agent-browser snapshot not piped through that redactor; (3) the corpus lint's S2 rule, which now prescribes a STRUCTURAL disclosure verbatim (use the filename: + redactor + shred form first; a refusal whose text starts `refused by playwright-mcp-redact-proxy:` means THAT server's registration is wrapped — any other error, such as the server's own File access denied, does not); (4) playwright-mcp-redact-proxy.py, a single-file stdio JSON-RPC relay that importlib-loads the redactor by path, runs redact_text over the text of EVERY tools/call result by shape (two tools inline tree lines on the pinned server — browser_snapshot and browser_find), appends --snapshot-mode none to the wrapped argv so action tools write no raw page-*.yml (and, only when started with the opt-in --chromium-fallback flag on a host with no Google Chrome executable, also appends --browser chromium --sandbox — not a sink flag; --no-sandbox, PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SANDBOX and config chromiumSandbox:false and --executable-path stay refused), refuses browser_snapshot with filename and any call carrying an undocumented _meta argument (measured: _meta.json returns the tree as one escaped string the line-anchored predicate cannot see), withholds a JSON-escaped tree in any result and an error carrying data or tree-shaped text, drops server notifications and every server request but roots/list, refuses to start on any launch setting that opens a raw sink around it (--save-session, a non-JSON or saveSession/saveVideo/server/non-vision-capabilities config, --port/--host, --caps beyond vision, --output-mode file, any DEBUG value that can enable a pw: logger, DEBUG_FILE), and is fail-closed in three arms with NO kill switch (cannot load or self-test the redactor → exit 2 before spawning; cannot rewrite a result → isError text that never quotes input; dead child → non-zero exit, closed stdin → group SIGTERM then SIGKILL, signalled to the GROUP even when the direct child has already exited). SHIPS vs WIRES: the plugin SHIPS the proxy and, since #8156, WIRES it — plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registers `playwright` through it (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*), alongside this repository's own .mcp.json; a customer's own registration stays wrapped only by their configuration. Residuals stay named, not closed: screenshots render a readonly credential panel in clear; browser_network_request / browser_evaluate / browser_run_code_unsafe return what they are asked for; console logs, PNGs and downloads are non-tree disk sinks; Page URL / title / dialog prose is inert to the predicate.

nodes.title: destructive-command guard

description.txt: ADR-277 (#9601, W2). plugins/soleur/hooks/destructive-command-guard.sh on `^Bash$`: lexes the command (bash -c, eval, $(...) and every list operator each yield their own simple command; quoted text and heredoc bodies are not commands) and answers DENY for a recursive rm of /, the home directory or an ancestor, and ASK for a recursive rm of the working directory or an ancestor, terraform/tofu destroy and apply -destroy, and a force-push or delete of a default branch (a small wrapper table plus the `--` suffix covers sudo, env, timeout, doppler run --). An unreadable envelope, a lexer failure or a bound trip asks; a missing jq or perl scans the raw envelope and asks on a hit (a raw-scan miss is an allow, stated). It never denies on a dependency failure. A deny also carries a top-level systemMessage because the person sees only a collapsed `Ran 1 shell command` otherwise (measured, CC 2.1.291). Kill switch SOLEUR_DISABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD=1, read from the harness environment (a settings env block can also set it: a seatbelt, not a boundary). Deliberately NOT decided: obfuscated or variable-built command names, xargs/find -delete, a script written then run, SQL, MCP delete tools, any non-Bash tool including Devin exec, Doppler secret writes, a plain terraform apply. NO EGRESS and no log: Soleur receives nothing and the hook writes nothing; the hook's output is persisted as a hook_success row in the customer's own harness transcript (the record of an answered Yes/No prompt is unmeasured). HOSTED POSTURE DIFFERS: it loads into hosted sessions like every plugin hook (settingSources:[] does not exclude hooks.json) and is disabled there by SOLEUR_DISABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD in AGENT_ENV_OVERRIDES, so W2 protects customer-machine plugin users, not hosted founders; hosted `canUseTool` asks, through a must-ask lane, before common forms of a default-branch force-push or delete, terraform or tofu destroy and a gh ref or repository delete (ADR-284, #9776), but it does not recognise every way of writing those commands, and for other destructive commands (rm -rf, git update-ref, other deletes) only a short blocklist that does not match them stands between the agent and the sandbox (ADR-093 amendment 2026-10-07, ADR-277 D8, ADR-284 residuals). The twelve server-side agent functions that spawn claude --plugin-dir plugins/soleur outside buildAgentEnv keep the guard ACTIVE (ADR-277, Server-side scheduled agents).

nodes.title: Shared git-data

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). BORN (ADR-149); the store is EMPTY until the LUKS cutover (#5274) flips `GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` (every write path is gated on that flag, #6976). The host reports its own boot correctness off-host (#6982, ADR-149 item 1): boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal, and gc faults to Better Stack. Since #9438 (ADR-283) it also pushes its own recurring liveness heartbeat (a 60 s timer that pings only while its local health checks pass; armed 2026-10-12 after a measured beat on the replaced host). The birth route is gated MECHANICALLY by `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate`, which refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template (a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload) and, since #8010, names a completed, successful `workflow_dispatch` run of the rehearsal workflow on `main` that uploaded a boot-evidence artifact and whose `head_sha` re-hashes to that evidence (resolved live through the GitHub REST API), with the Sentry cross-check verdict required in the file. CI root access for the cutover is ADR-220's (see the github -> gitDataStore edge). AT REST: from PR1 of #8211 (ADR-239) the render ALWAYS serves the LUKS mapper `/dev/mapper/git-data` (`hcloud_volume.git_data_luks`, git-data-luks.tf) at `/mnt/git-data`, from boot — there is no plaintext/LUKS selector and no runtime repoint, and the serving change reached production through an ordinary `git_data_host_replace` (ADR-237 post-merge step 3) while the store was empty and `GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` was off. The first such replace (2026-09-24) destroyed the last host that served the PLAINTEXT ext4 `hcloud_volume.git_data` (`format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) and FATALed on that volume's dirty journal; the replace carrying the forward fix (ADR-239 amendment 2026-09-24) booted a host on 2026-09-25 (run 36118115758) that serves the still-empty store from the LUKS mapper (ADR-239 accepted 2026-09-27). The retired plaintext volume was deleted at the provider API on 2026-10-27 (ADR-239 Amendment 2026-10-27) and its ledger exception is retired. The bootstrap's plaintext arm stays (ADR-239 Amendment 2026-10-28): once per instance it sets any plaintext device kernel read-only and reads it through a throwaway dm snapshot whose copy-on-write lives in RAM (ADR-239 amendment 2026-09-24), only to prove its post-journal-replay tree holds no repository (the arm's design purpose, not a finding about the deleted device), and while the literal volume id remains a host rebirth boots into the `plaintext_unverified` FATAL (ADR-239 Amendment 2026-10-26, item 4); the host replace, rotate and create gates no longer demand the retired plaintext addresses, and each route refuses through a plaintext-id interlock until that literal is blanked (ADR-239 Amendment 2026-10-28). Every store-acting script refuses unless `findmnt -n -o SOURCE --mountpoint /mnt/git-data` EQUALS the mapper and the bootstrap has written /etc/git-data/store-verified. Since #8210 the LUKS mapper is reopened on EVERY boot by a systemd oneshot that fetches the passphrase from Doppler at boot (never from disk), so the store survives a reboot rather than silently vanishing at the first one

nodes.title: Workspace Git Data (/workspaces)

description.txt: Every user's checked-out repository. SOLE-COPY: refs/checkpoints/* is pushed by no refspec, session-sync.ts autocommits only knowledge-base/**, and signup-provisioned workspaces have no git remote at all — so ADR-068 §1's 'GitHub remains the durable rehydration source' does NOT hold here and there is no durable second copy anywhere (no upstream to rehydrate from). ENCRYPTED AT REST as of the 2026-07-23 cutover — the gap #6588/ADR-119 opened (PLAINTEXT ext4 while the published privacy policy claimed LUKS) is closed. HISTORY: an earlier 2026-07-20 cutover attempt (run 29782780158) landed /mnt/data on crypto_LUKS for ~27 minutes before its own dead-man timer silently remounted the retained plaintext volume over it (#6812) — do not cite that landing as the current state. The 2026-07-23 cutover is the one that certified: `workspaces-luks-verify` run **30040444418** reported `SOLEUR_WORKSPACES_READYZ ready=true writable=true populated=true workspace_count=8 expected=8` against `/dev/mapper/workspaces` — a mechanically measured verdict, not an assumed one (this distinction, per ADR-140, is the whole feature). web-2's instance was knowingly left plaintext (never served, empty) until its 2026-07-17 teardown (#6538/#6463). The fleet was single-host when this was written, so no plaintext member remained — but that was a statement about the fleet at the time, NOT an invariant, and it no longer holds: var.web_hosts has two keys since the cattle web-2 was born 2026-07-27 (#6969). The fresh web-2 (repinned cpx22, #6966) has its own per-host workspaces volume (hcloud_volume.workspaces, web-2 key). UNTIL ITS LIVE CONVERSION that volume is still the empty, Hetzner-formatted PLAINTEXT ext4 volume it was born with. A volume born from the template is RAW and is formatted guest-side LUKS2 at first boot by the baked provisioner (ADR-263, #6931, which supersedes the deferral in ADR-143 R3), and web-2 becomes LUKS-backed at boot only after its single-use gated rebirth has run and the daily probe has read crypto_LUKS on the live host - not before. [Updated 2026-10-11 (#9372): web-2's volume was replaced on 2026-10-06 and is now LUKS-formatted and opened by the running instance, and the ledger row reads luks; that is formatted/opened plus green probes, not a reopen test, and web-2 holds no data and stays at serving weight 0.] The workspaces_luks attachment stays web-1-bound and outside the birth fan-out (#6964), so web-host-create refuses web-1 by name. That member holds NO user data (sole copy is web-1's volume; web-2 is never routed pre-flip, dns.tf app record is web-1-only and the #6575 anti-pooling gate fail-closes), and it MUST NOT take serving weight while plaintext — re-evaluate at the ADR-068 Phase-3 GA flip. SOLE COPY FROM #6604 step 7 (2026-10-08): PR #9348 merges only after the wipe dispatch D has concluded with delete_issued=true on web-1's retained pre-cutover plaintext copy (hcloud_volume.workspaces web-1 key, Hetzner volume 105149570, frozen at the 2026-07-23 cutover), which D zeroes with a full-device read-back, detaches and deletes (destruction record: knowledge-base/legal/audits/workspaces-plaintext-destruction-record.md). From that deletion this LUKS volume (hcloud_volume.workspaces_luks, 106443278) is the ONLY copy of every workspace, with no backup or snapshot (#5274, #8625); since the merge of PR #9348 Terraform declares prevent_destroy + delete_protection on it and prevent_destroy on its attachment (the Hetzner-side delete protection is effective after the post-merge SSH-stage apply), and web-1 owns no plaintext workspaces volume (only web-2's instance remains, serving-weight 0, intended empty, #6931)

description.txt: DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner. Since #11181/PR #11766 it also carries the GA LOAD BALANCER on app.soleur.ai (ADR-068 §(b)): cloudflare_load_balancer.app overlays the retained A record (fallback for a disabled LB), default+fallback pool web_1 {web-1@1 serving, web-2@1 serving since the 2026-11 serve flip (#12167); drain is an explicit ga-pool-update act}, health monitor http/:80 /health (the Flexible-SSL edge path; the https/:443 create shape probed a port with no listener and reported every origin down under the self-fallback), origin_steering random, plus a load_balancing_health_alert notification policy. Updates ride cf-lb-overlay.yml ga-monitor-fix/ga-pool-update arms — never the routine apply.

@playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha), spawned by npx as a stdio JSON-RPC child — one newline-terminated JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (measured) — driving a HEADED real Chrome (channel chrome, chromiumSandbox true, X11 forced at the env level) on the operator workstation with the persistent profile ~/.cache/playwright-mcp-profile (this repository's registration claims it, or a numbered sibling directory when it is held, by a kernel flock tied to the proxy process — slot 0 may wait up to 7 s, for the same session's previous launch or an unknown/unreadable owner — so a new-style launch or /mcp reconnect kills nothing; an old-style launch string still running in another worktree can, and the plugin registration has no lease), whose password manager autofills into pages the agent opens. An accessibility snapshot serialises the VALUE of every input, so a bare browser_snapshot on a login page or a credential panel returns the value inline in the tool result. Since #7980 the agent runtime reaches this server THROUGH the plugin's snapshotGuard component rather than directly — that relay is the trust boundary this node exists to show — and only on a registration that routes through it: this repository's .mcp.json does, and since #8156 the plugin's own plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registration does by default (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*, on the dedicated soleur-playwright-mcp-profile under the XDG cache root — that registration ships NO config and no display forcing, so it runs the upstream defaults: headed, channel chrome; on a host with no Google Chrome executable its opt-in --chromium-fallback proxy flag makes the proxy append --browser chromium --sandbox, so Playwright launches its bundled Chromium instead with the Chromium sandbox kept on (a host that cannot run it fails closed: install Google Chrome), and its env carries only PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS=0, an inert guard on stdio, not the fix for anything — ADR-271); a customer's own registration does not unless they route it themselves; the hosted agent-runner registers no Playwright server (the vendored plugin tree excludes the plugin-root .mcp.json — both vendor steps rm it post-copy, so the hosted plugins:[type local] load never discovers it); the Inngest fleet's per-fire cron-ux-audit overlay runs a SEPARATE 0.0.75 copy, UNWRAPPED, with --snapshot-mode none appended directly (register PA-31 §(g)). Every behaviour cited is a dated observation of the pinned version, not an undertaking about the tool; the suite derives its fixture directory from the pin, so a bump without a re-capture reddens.

Durable trigger layer for server-side agents — cron, oneshot, and HTTP-armed reminders. Extracted to its own single-host private-net node so exactly-one-scheduler is enforced by topology, unblocking active-active web (ADR-030, ADR-100, #6178). The CLI binary is version-pinned in inngest.tf (inngest_cli_version + per-arch sha256, verified against ONE upstream checksums.txt at pin time) with a named freshness owner since #7463: the rule-audit.yml poll detects drift, inngest-cli-staleness.test.sh enforces coherence, inngest-cli.provenance.md is the analysis of record. ADOPTING (#10136, ADR-294): a host-level stunnel4 systemd unit (soleur-inngest-tls.service, not a process inside the Inngest process and not a dependency of it) terminates TLS on 10.0.1.40:8443 and forwards to 127.0.0.1:8288; the legacy plaintext :8288 listener stays open and counted until a later replace

OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. SUPERSEDED BY #9252 (read the v2.1.20 statements above as the 2026-08-12 record): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.22 from the merge of that PR, and the host will run it once the registry-host-replace that merge fires completes; the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows then report zot_image_digest=46f688dc2631. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Booted (since #8714 step 5.3b-iii, 2026-09-28) from the pinned GitHub release asset that mirrors the upstream image byte-for-byte, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement), and never from ghcr.io, which the host name-resolution-denies (see the zotRegistry -> github edge). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-09-20 (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The preceding CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING clause, which asserted the live device was unencrypted pending an unfired `registry-luks-recut` (#6929), is RETRACTED 2026-09-20 (#8386) — and it was already spent when written, since the recut fired 2026-08-10, as the pinned-image clause above this one records. What settled it is an off-host measurement rather than a job log: since #8386 the SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK heartbeat carries store_mount_src / store_backing_dev / store_mount_devid / store_expected_devid / store_luks in its trusted region, and boot b3ec6c3b (delivered by registry-host-replace run 35489418603) reads store_luks=yes with store_mount_devid == store_expected_devid == scsi-0HC_Volume_106585109 across 120 rows. encryption-posture-ledger.json's `hcloud_volume.registry` row therefore reads live_verification: available. Read the heartbeat, not this description, whenever the two could diverge. Scope: that measurement says the store SITS ON a LUKS container, not that the passphrase still opens it (the escrow re-test and the standing alert are #8408), and the reboot window in which zot could serve a root-fs directory is measured and graded (the registry_store_not_luks alert). Since #8408 zot start is gated on the LUKS filesystem's sentinel on EVERY container start (a --mount bind of /var/lib/zot/.soleur-luks-sentinel; the NIC guard starts it within one tick once the store returns), and the passphrase is re-tested daily (store_escrow= on SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK) — both delivered on boot 5639cc07 (registry-host-replace run 35672138112, 2026-09-22; PR #8456); read the heartbeat for the live answer. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.

description.txt: Inngest durable queue + run-state. AOF on the persistent volume survives a host re-provision — the durable-backend umbrella #5450. AT REST: LUKS-ENCRYPTED since the additive cutover of 2026-09-20 (#8296). The live store is hcloud_volume.inngest_redis_luks, opened as mapper inngest-redis and mounted at /mnt/data; the passphrase is minted at merge and held in Doppler (inngest-redis-luks.tf), and inngest-luks-open.service reopens the mapper on every boot. The encryption-posture ledger records that row as mechanism luks. SOLE COPY: since 2026-10-09 this volume and the Doppler key INNGEST_REDIS_LUKS_KEY are the only copy of the store, and the key is the only opener the host reads (an independent copy of the passphrase sits in Terraform state), because the retained plaintext backstop (the pre-cutover volume hcloud_volume.inngest_redis, id 106261946) was detached, zeroed with a read-back and destroyed under #8285 (Hetzner answered 404 at 2026-10-09T16:21:26Z). That erasure is logical, guest-side and self-attested, not physical; op=luks-rollback is retired (on the merge of PR #9877) because there is no plaintext volume to roll back to. PROTECTION (#9879, ADR-282 accepted 2026-10-15; delete-protection flag read back once, prevent_destroy is plan-time only): Hetzner delete protection and prevent_destroy on the volume, prevent_destroy on the passphrase pair and on the two Doppler cascade parents, the attachment deliberately unpinned so the sanctioned host replace still works, and guards over Terraform text, workflow reachability and removed/moved blocks. RESIDUALS: protection defends against mistaken deletes, not against a holder of the read/write Hetzner token or the Doppler tokens that can overwrite the key; the ciphertext and the LUKS header have no backup; no sanctioned erase path exists. A probe row reporting /mnt/data on anything other than the encrypted volume pages via logtail_exploration_alert.inngest_luks_wrong_volume, and the daily follow-through probe that cross-checked the ledger claim against the device was retired 2026-10-12 (#9703 Stage 3b). KEY CONTINUITY (#9927 item 2, ADR-282 addendum 2026-10-26): once the owner has delivered the signed bundle that carries it, an on-host probe, daily while healthy and hourly while not ok (SOLEUR_INNGEST_LUKS_KEY_PROBE, a luksOpen --test-passphrase read with the host-held key; no mapper opened, nothing written to the volume) pages on verdict=fail_ when that key no longer opens a keyslot of the header, which narrows the earlier gap where header damage was detected only at the first Redis failure; it does NOT detect damage that leaves the held key working, a fault arriving after the probe ran, or a Doppler copy that differs from the host file, it creates no header backup, and it recovers nothing (no recovery exists if the header is lost). A probe pipeline that goes silent reads as healthy to the alert, so #8516 added the dead-man's-switch sibling betteruptime_heartbeat.inngest_server_probe (uptime-alerts.tf — born paused; its feeder is scheduled-inngest-probe-heartbeat.yml, which beats it only on a fresh dedicated probe row and sends nothing while it is paused, armed 2026-10-12: read-back status=up, feeder runs verdict=beat, #9703). The authority for which volume holds the store is the durable pointer INNGEST_LUKS_ACTIVE_VOLUME_ID, not a signature on a device (ADR-142).

PRIVATE GHCR registry (ghcr.io/jikig-ai/soleur-web-platform + soleur-inngest-bootstrap) — the ORIGINAL host pull source, now WRITE-ONLY: still dual-pushed by CI, but DEAD AS A FALLBACK since the Phase-5 retirement — the read PAT is revoked (GET api.github.com/user -> 401) and the minter was disabled (GHCR_MINTER_DISABLED=true; pull-token mint -> 403 DENIED), verified 2026-07-30 (#7071); the minter, the PAT variables and their Doppler keys were deleted by ADR-096 task 5.4 (#8714). It receives every image and can serve none of its PRIVATE packages TO HOSTS (the host pull of the PUBLIC cosign verifier image was a separate edge until #8714 moved it to gcr.io — `hetzner -> sigstore`). Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. SINCE #8036 1c (2026-09-23) THE DEPLOY-PATH HOST-SIDE CODE IS DELETED, not merely dead, AND SINCE #8036 1d (2026-09-24, ADR-096 5.3b-i) THE FRESH-BOOT CODE TOO: no host presents a GHCR credential at boot — the web and inngest templates and the baked bootstrap script carry no GHCR login and no GHCR pull, and no templatefile() passes the GHCR credential into user_data (true of the templates at merge; of each host once it is replaced from them). The inngest templates keep the ghcr.io/…soleur-inngest-bootstrap tag@sha256 literal only as the bump bot's pin carrier; it is never pulled. ci-deploy.sh has no `docker login ghcr.io`, no auth-recovery re-fetch and no fallback branch, and it sweeps the revoked inline credential out of the deploy docker config on every deploy. So “dead edge” is now a statement about code that no longer exists rather than about a credential that cannot authenticate. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION (#11424, ADR-096 amendment 2026-10-28): soleur:registry-breakglass-mirror is the sanctioned MANUAL exception — an operator-driven break-glass pull that presents an operator-supplied read:packages PAT and scopes name resolution per-command via `curl --resolve` past the hosts-file sinkhole (zero persistent config, no standing credential, no host code path), so “dead edge” names the absence of a STANDING pull capability and is not absolute against a deliberate human procedure. Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).

The PUBLIC upstream release surface (github.com/inngest/inngest) that publishes the self-hosted `inngest` binary — release tags, per-arch tarballs (inngest_<ver>_linux_{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz), and one release-shipped checksums.txt per version. Reached by two consumers with different trust semantics: the dedicated host's bootstrap downloads the version the committed `inngest_cli_version` pin names and sha256-verifies the tarball against the committed per-arch checksum before executing it (the reviewed embed in inngest.tf is the trust anchor, not the checksums file — it is a plain sha256sum manifest, not GPG-signed), and CI reaches it twice (build-inngest-bootstrap-image.yml downloads the same pinned tarball for the bootstrap image; the `Detect inngest CLI pin drift` poll in rule-audit.yml reads the releases listing to measure the pinned-version delta, #7463). Added 2026-09-29 (#7463) because the edge was unmodeled while the pin sat 29 stable releases behind with no freshness owner — the gap #7308 named. FRESHNESS OWNER (mirrors the projectZot/node discipline): no bot mutates the pin; detection is the rule-audit.yml poll (1st + 15th — files one idempotent `inngest-pin-drift` issue); enforcement is apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-cli-staleness.test.sh in deploy-script-tests; the analysis of record is apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-cli.provenance.md; the sub-second liveness probe is inngest-cli-pin-probe.sh.

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. The read direction is unchanged and is still the ONLY thing that grades a CI-emitted marker: the emitter's exit code is not evidence, so a run is green only after it reads its own run_id back out through the ClickHouse path (ADR-172 §2). Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and at the time a vendor-page reading put the object pool at 10/10 (no cap is asserted any more: since #7884/ADR-222 the twice-daily heartbeat-live-reconcile prints SOLEUR_HEARTBEAT_RECONCILE_INVENTORY monitors=<n> heartbeats=<n> total=<n>, and live held 4 monitors + 9 heartbeats = 13 objects on 2026-09-15; re-measured read-only 2026-10-22 for #10455 b: 7 monitors + 12 heartbeats = 19 objects, 21 once the per-host web_bash_synthetic pair is born). git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness (soleur-registry-prd) is armed: its on-host feeder shipped in #6537 and the monitor reads up/unpaused (re-measured 2026-09-24). All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). The #5933 Item 1 per-host origin absence detector (betteruptime_monitor.web_host on web-N hostnames) is RETIRED: the origin answers only the app.soleur.ai Host, so the probe read CF 521, and betteruptime_monitor.app replaced it (uptime-alerts.tf). SINCE #7884/ADR-222 betteruptime_monitor.app_health ('soleur app database readiness', the adopted hand-made monitor 4226366) is a KEYWORD monitor on https://app.soleur.ai/health that pages when the body stops containing the compact-JSON pair supabase:connected — /health answers HTTP 200 in every database state, so the body is the only signal of a database outage. SINCE #7798/ADR-204 IT ALSO OWNS A PROPERTY SENTRY STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS: betteruptime_monitor.soleur_www_redirect ('soleur dot ai www redirect 301', uptime-alerts.tf) asserts that https://www.soleur.ai/ returns exactly 301 WITHOUT following it (follow_redirects = false, remember_cookies = false — the vendor rejects a 3xx expectation with either enabled, HTTP 422). Sentry's uptime checker always follows 3xx and grades the FINAL response, so its predecessor sentry_uptime_monitor.soleur_www asserted `equals 301` against the apex's 200 -- an assertion it CANNOT satisfy (structural; the measurement behind it is 10/10 most recent checks failing on 2026-09-07, not a paged-back 101-day census). That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. SINCE #8364 the same no-follow capability carries THREE SAMPLED deep-URL 301 probes, one per independent edge-redirect mechanism, all expected_status_codes=[301] with follow_redirects=false: betteruptime_monitor.seo_redirect_zone_ruleset ('soleur pages agents redirect 301', https://soleur.ai/pages/agents.html — covers a lost rules{} block in cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects), betteruptime_monitor.seo_redirect_bulk_item ('soleur legal privacy redirect 301', https://soleur.ai/pages/legal/privacy-policy.html — covers an emptied cloudflare_list.legal_redirects or a dropped explicit item) and betteruptime_monitor.seo_redirect_blog_pair ('soleur blog dated slug redirect 301', https://soleur.ai/blog/2026-03-16-soleur-vs-anthropic-cowork/ — covers the generated blog_redirect_pairs expansion end-to-end). SAMPLED, not exhaustive — three probes is the smallest set separating the three failure mechanisms; probe-URL membership in the declared redirect source set is pinned by infra/seo-redirect-monitors.test.sh. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage). Since #10453 a second sandbox alert, soleur-faithful-canary-sandbox-broken-prd, pages on the deploy-time SDK Bash smoke verdict sdk_bash_smoke_failed that ci-deploy.sh journals on a canary (email only; the Slack wake of ADR-260 is not provable from the API, see the canary-probe-set runbook).
Slack workspace — Better Stack incident-alert target (native integration); mobile push to the operator is the primary wake path, email retained as secondary (#9168, ADR-260).

description.txt: plugins/soleur/ — skills, agents, knowledge base, AND the shared bash primitives shipped for execution on an installed user's machine (ADR-178, #7409): scripts/lib/session-state.sh is the cross-session lock/lease layer that gates worktree reaping AND, since #8400, branch deletion: `cleanup-merged` keys its lease check on the BRANCH rather than on a worktree path, so a merged branch whose worktree was already removed is now held by a live lease instead of reaching `git push origin --delete` and `git branch -D`. The narrower wording was falsified by that change, in the same way and at the same time as the script's own fail-closed banner. It lived under .claude/hooks/ until #7409, i.e. outside the subtree marketplace.json copies, so every installed user ran with that layer silently replaced by no-op stubs. What this system SHIPS is therefore not only prose for an agent to read — it includes executable concurrency primitives whose absence is unobservable to the user. Since ADR-254 (#8880) it also ships a user-machine WRITE surface: `scripts/emit-decision.sh` appends field-allowlisted decision records to the project-local `.soleur/decisions.jsonl` (NO-ECHO metadata only, `.soleur/.gitignore` self-guard, ~5 MB rotation, tester-owned, no egress — the aggregate reaches Jikigai only when a tester runs `alpha-metrics.sh` and pastes it at checkpoint). Since ADR-264 it also ships the staged, agent-runnable operator-script contract (`scripts/lib/operator-script.sh`: --list, --stage, --stage --apply --plan-digest, exit 75) and the PreToolUse hook `hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh` registered in `hooks/hooks.json`, which reaches a founder's install and is loaded by web Concierge too (the web runtime opts it out until the web approval adapter lands). A further write surface lands with #9403 (ADR-268): `scripts/pipeline-tally.sh` mutates per-branch work-unit counters under `<git-common>/soleur-session-state/counters/` (key=value, flock-serialized, units only — never dollars) and `hooks/stop-hook.sh` READS the ledger's `capped` key as a hard-cap floor; the ledger is repo-local machine state with no egress, and ship renders its counts into the public PR body as a `## Pipeline Tally` section. Since ADR-250 Amendment 2 (#9677) `cleanup-merged` can also, on explicit opt-in, delete expired entries from the plugin's own scratch-quarantine directory under /tmp and /var/tmp (`SOLEUR_QUARANTINE_DRAIN=1`, a terminal delete on the user's machine scoped to that directory) and prune old Docker build cache and dangling images (`SOLEUR_DOCKER_PRUNE`, dry-run first, never volumes or containers); both print stdout markers (on a user's machine they stay there; the web platform's telemetry mirror forwards them like every other SOLEUR_* marker). Since ADR-277 (#9601, W2) it also ships a second PreToolUse hook, `hooks/destructive-command-guard.sh` (with the Perl lexer `hooks/lib/shell-argv.pl`), that asks or denies before a destructive terraform/tofu, default-branch force-push or recursive delete of `/` or home reaches a customer's shell; it sends nothing and writes nothing, and hosted web sessions opt it out through SOLEUR_DISABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD (server-side scheduled agents keep it active), so it protects customer-machine users, not hosted founders (hosted sessions ask separately, through a must-ask lane in canUseTool for common forms of a default-branch force-push or delete, terraform destroy and a gh delete, ADR-284; the lane does not recognise every spelling). Since ADR-290 Amendment 1 (#10331, slice 2) it also ships a user-repository surface: `plugins/soleur/scripts/lint-ratchet.py` user mode inspects any git repository it is run in (it reads root and tracked nested ruff configs and the baseline path, with no install and no ruff run unless a tracked ruff config AND a baseline file are present), and on an opted-in repository or an explicit --update executes a sha256-pinned ruff wheel it downloads once into a per-user 0700 cache outside the repository (PyPI over TLS, deliberately not modelled as an element); it writes `.lint-ratchet/ruff.baseline.txt` only on an explicit --update; it sends nothing to Soleur; the hosted image has no python3, so the call is a skip there.

nodes.title: Hook Engine

description.txt: Guards tool calls (blocks commits to main, rm -rf, etc.) AND injects additive context — phase-surface hints (ADR-070) and declarative skill context_queries (ADR-086). CONSUMES a MODEL-CONTROLLED tool-call envelope on stdin: that input is untrusted and is parsed without shell evaluation, with each contracted field type-asserted rather than coerced (ADR-156, #7164 — an array tool_input.command previously reached eval AND evaded every anchored guard). The repo-local Stop arm consumes `last_assistant_message`, equally model-controlled and type-asserted: it fails open on any parse doubt (the ADR-157 supersession note), blocks at most once per turn, shares `lib/technical-fork-cues.sh` with the pre-ask gate and never runs in web (`settingSources:[]`). Prior description said only what hooks DO, never what they CONSUME. A PreToolUse hook also has a THIRD disposition beyond allow/deny: it may REWRITE tool_input before execution and let the call proceed (ADR-162, #7165) — grep-rewrite.sh prepends a grep() redefinition that neutralizes the ugrep shim which reached 9.5 GB RSS against a 21 kB file, leaving the command byte-identical. Bounded by a SINGLE-REWRITER invariant: updatedInput REPLACES tool_input (it does not merge), a sibling deny still wins, and permission rules match the ORIGINAL command. Since ADR-264 there are exactly TWO named rewriters: the shipped plugin hook `plugins/soleur/hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh` turns the harness approval prompt into the human acknowledgement of a generated operator script's production write — it recognises the script by its `SOLEUR-GENERATED-OPERATOR-SCRIPT v2` header content, mints a one-time command-bound receipt (a record named sha256(nonce) under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/soleur/approvals`, 0700/0600, 10-minute expiry, local state with no persistent store), rewrites the command to carry the nonce, and answers ask (interactive), defer then a resume marker (headless), or deny (bypass modes, unknown mode); it FAILS CLOSED for a candidate command and never for a non-candidate, and the web runtime opts it out via SOLEUR_DISABLE_OPERATOR_STAGE_APPROVAL_HOOK=1 from buildAgentEnv (ADR-162 amendment 2026-10-01). The receipt is a same-user file: it resists an instruction-following agent, not a hijacked one. Additionally, in the repo-local `.claude/` hook surface only — never the shipped plugin surface — it enforces host resource control: at SessionStart it adopts the agent process tree into a memory-capped systemd transient scope (ADR-161). Since ADR-261 (#9239) that backstop's DISPATCH is version-independent: settings.json execs a stable resolver shim (memory-backstop-resolve.sh) that selects the highest-BACKSTOP_REVISION copy across the checkout, the managed path ~/.local/share/soleur/hooks/, and the two plugin caches; a strictly-newer winner self-publishes to the managed path (flock-serialized) BEFORE exec, the schema:2 ledger records resolved_from/backstop_revision/repaired, and repair_stale_scopes runtime-converges stale-adopted scope caps at any SessionStart (ADR-159 applied to transient scopes). The resolver itself cannot self-upgrade — a stale checkout keeps its stale shim — but sweep-repair still reaches the scopes a stale shim's hook created. That surface split is scoped to resource control and must not be read as a general one: since ADR-227 (#8323) the SHIPPED plugin surface is itself a compaction-lifecycle consumer AND, for the first time, STATEFUL ACROSS EVENTS: `hooks/compaction-state.sh` writes a per-session ledger under `${TMPDIR}/soleur-compaction/` at `PreCompact` and reads it at `SessionStart:compact`. Every other hook here is a stateless single-event transformer, so this is a new property of the container rather than a new instance of an existing one. The ledger is machine-local, session-keyed, mode 0700, reaped at 7 days, and deliberately outside the user git tree — `hooks/compaction-state.sh` binds `PreCompact` and `SessionStart:compact`, so a customer install now carries hook code that runs on events the repo-local surface never handled. Because a plugin hook is global, that consumer is gated on a two-conjunct scope guard (a `plugins/soleur` directory AND a Soleur plan/spec artifact) rather than on `is-inside-work-tree`, which is true in every customer repo. Where this container runs server-side there is no per-user systemd bus, so that path declines and does nothing. HARNESS SURFACES: `.claude/hooks/` (Claude Code) is the only tree of hook CODE since 2026-09-23 (ADR-245, #8306), which retired the hand-ported PreToolUse mirrors; ADR-165's split-by-reason-class posture described those mirrors and is historical. One hook PREDICATE does have a second implementation outside this tree: the filing gate's `lib/filing-shape.pl` classifier is mirrored by `filingShape()` in the cron containment hook (apps/web-platform/server/inngest/cron-bash-allowlist-hook.mjs), and the two are bound only by the shared corpus `lib/filing-shape-corpus.json`, which both suites run (ADR-256, #9089). Dispatch REGISTRIES are per-harness and audited (#8205, ADR-223): `.claude/settings.json` is Claude-canonical (its lowercase `^write$`/`^ask_user_question$` twins serve Grok and coincidentally cover those tools under Devin), `.devin/config.json` binds the triaged hook set on anchored Devin wire names (Claude matchers there are loaded-but-dead), `.codex/config.toml` serves its harness, and `.claude/hooks/devin-dispositions.tsv` + `devin-matcher-parity.test.sh` keep the audit honest. On the `.claude` side exit 0 is the precondition for that posture at all: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout JSON entirely (#7190). That single-tree statement describes where hook CODE lives; since ADR-178 (#7409) it no longer describes where its concurrency layer comes from — `lib/incidents.sh`, `lib/log-rotation.sh` and `pre-merge-rebase.sh` source the session-state lock/lease primitives from a THIRD, shipped location inside the deployed plugin root, reaching in from the repo side. Its TELEMETRY has a namespace contract (ADR-205, #7853): an emitted rule_id carrying a section prefix (hr/wg/cq/rf/pdr/cm) CLAIMS membership in the AGENTS corpus and is orphan-checked against it; one carrying no prefix is hook telemetry and is outside the corpus by construction, which replaced nine hand-maintained exemption stanzas in rule-metrics-aggregate.sh. Under test the sink is redirected at the RUNNER CHOKEPOINT — both bunfig preloads, the vitest globalSetup, the test-helpers.sh prelude and the _git_fixture_env import — never at the call site, and never by teaching this container to detect tests, because a false positive there would darken real operator telemetry.

nodes.title: destructive-command guard

description.txt: ADR-277 (#9601, W2). plugins/soleur/hooks/destructive-command-guard.sh on `^Bash$`: lexes the command (bash -c, eval, $(...) and every list operator each yield their own simple command; quoted text and heredoc bodies are not commands) and answers DENY for a recursive rm of /, the home directory or an ancestor, and ASK for a recursive rm of the working directory or an ancestor, terraform/tofu destroy and apply -destroy, and a force-push or delete of a default branch (a small wrapper table plus the `--` suffix covers sudo, env, timeout, doppler run --). An unreadable envelope, a lexer failure or a bound trip asks; a missing jq or perl scans the raw envelope and asks on a hit (a raw-scan miss is an allow, stated). It never denies on a dependency failure. A deny also carries a top-level systemMessage because the person sees only a collapsed `Ran 1 shell command` otherwise (measured, CC 2.1.291). Kill switch SOLEUR_DISABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD=1, read from the harness environment (a settings env block can also set it: a seatbelt, not a boundary). Deliberately NOT decided: obfuscated or variable-built command names, xargs/find -delete, a script written then run, SQL, MCP delete tools, any non-Bash tool including Devin exec, Doppler secret writes, a plain terraform apply. NO EGRESS and no log: Soleur receives nothing and the hook writes nothing; the hook's output is persisted as a hook_success row in the customer's own harness transcript (the record of an answered Yes/No prompt is unmeasured). HOSTED POSTURE DIFFERS: it loads into hosted sessions like every plugin hook (settingSources:[] does not exclude hooks.json) and is disabled there by SOLEUR_DISABLE_DESTRUCTIVE_GUARD in AGENT_ENV_OVERRIDES, so W2 protects customer-machine plugin users, not hosted founders; hosted `canUseTool` asks, through a must-ask lane, before common forms of a default-branch force-push or delete, terraform or tofu destroy and a gh ref or repository delete (ADR-284, #9776), but it does not recognise every way of writing those commands, and for other destructive commands (rm -rf, git update-ref, other deletes) only a short blocklist that does not match them stands between the agent and the sandbox (ADR-093 amendment 2026-10-07, ADR-277 D8, ADR-284 residuals). The twelve server-side agent functions that spawn claude --plugin-dir plugins/soleur outside buildAgentEnv keep the guard ACTIVE (ADR-277, Server-side scheduled agents).
